1.1Chapter 1 — AI Foundations

AI kya hai — Weak AI vs Strong AI

AI ka matlab hai — computer aise kaam kare jo pehle sirf insaan kar sakta tha: seekhna, samajhna, faisla lena. Lekin aaj ki AI aur filmon wali AI mein zameen-aasmaan ka farak hai.

Science-fiction filmon mein AI aksar ek super-intelligent robot hota hai jo insaanon se behtar sochta hai. Asliyat mein aaj ki AI Weak AI hai — matlab ek khaas kaam mein mahir, jaise chehre pehchanna ya gaadi chalana. Woh us kaam ke bahar kuch nahi jaanti.

Strong AI (ya AGI — Artificial General Intelligence) woh hoti jo insaan ki tarah har cheez samajh sake, khule aam baat-cheet kar sake aur naye kaam khud seekh le. Aaj tak koi Strong AI bani nahi hai.

Ek mashhoor tech company ke co-founder ne AI ko "ultimate Google" kaha tha — ek aisi system jo har sawaal ka jawab de sake. Yeh sapna abhi door hai, lekin Weak AI ne hi duniya badal di hai.

Is chapter mein hum AI ki poori kahani dekhenge — 1936 se lekar aaj tak: Turing Test, AI Winter, Expert Systems aur Neural Networks ki wapsi.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 1

1.2Chapter 1 — AI Foundations

Turing Test — machine kab intelligent kehlayegi?

1950 mein ek ganit-shaastri ne ek simple sawaal poocha: machine kab intelligent mani jayegi? Unka jawab tha — jab woh baat-cheet mein insaan se pehchani na ja sake.

1936 mein [Name] ne "On Computable Numbers" paper likha aur Turing Machine ka idea diya — ek aisi theoretical machine jo koi bhi calculation kar sakti thi. Yeh aaj ke computer ka neev hai.

1950 mein unhone "Computing Machinery and Intelligence" paper mein Turing Test diya. Ismein 3 players hote hain: ek judge, ek insaan aur ek computer — teeno alag kamron mein. Judge dono se sawaal poochta hai. Agar judge bata na sake ki kaun insaan hai aur kaun computer, to computer ne test pass kar liya.

2014 mein ek program ne daava kiya ki usne test pass kar liya — usne khud ko 13 saal ka ladka bataya tha. Lekin experts ne is par sawaal uthaye, kyunki bachche se galtiyan expected hoti hain.

May 2018 mein ek badi tech company ke voice assistant ne hairdresser ko call karke appointment book ki — itni natural awaaz mein ki saamne wale ko pata hi nahi chala ki woh machine se baat kar raha hai. Lekin yeh bhi poora pass nahi tha, kyunki baat-cheet pehle se tay (scripted) thi, khuli hui nahi.

Loebner Prize ek saalana competition hai jismein chatbots Turing Test pass karne ki koshish karte hain. Aaj tak koi bhi system poori tarah se test pass nahi kar paya hai.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 1

1.3Chapter 1 — AI Foundations

Chinese Room — kya machine sach mein samajhti hai?

Ek philosopher ne 1980 mein "Minds, Brains, and Programs" paper mein ek mashhoor thought experiment diya: Chinese Room. Iska sawaal tha — kya machine sach mein samajhti hai, ya sirf nakal karti hai?

Imagine karo: ek aadmi ek kamre mein band hai. Uske paas Chinese likhe hue cards aate hain, aur uske paas ek rule-book hai jo batati hai ki kis card ka kya jawab dena hai. Aadmi ko Chinese bilkul nahi aati, lekin rule-book follow karke woh sahi jawab de deta hai. Bahar wale ko lagega ki andar wala Chinese samajhta hai — lekin sach mein woh sirf rules follow kar raha hai.

Isi tarah, philosopher ka kehna tha ki computer bhi sirf symbols ko rules se jodta hai — woh samajhta nahi hai. Yeh Strong AI (sach mein samajhne wali) aur Weak AI (sirf pattern match karne wali) ke beech ka farak hai.

Strong AI ka matlab hai — machine ko consciousness ho, woh sach mein samjhe. Weak AI ka matlab hai — machine ek khaas kaam kare, jaise voice assistant sawaal ka jawab de, lekin usko uska matlab pata na ho.

Doosre tests bhi propose hue hain. Kurzweil–Kapor Test mein machine ko 2 ghante tak baat karni hoti hai aur 3 mein se 2 judges ko dhokha dena hota hai — target saal 2029 rakha gaya tha. Coffee Test mein robot ko kisi anjaan ke ghar jaakar kitchen dhoondhni hai aur coffee banani hai — yeh aaj bhi bahut mushkil hai.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 1

1.4Chapter 1 — AI Foundations

Dimaag ek machine hai? — 1943 ka paper

AI ki neev dimaag ko samajhne se padi. 1943 mein ek paper "A Logical Calculus of the Ideas Immanent in Nervous Activity" ne dikhaya ki neurons logic gates ki tarah kaam karte hain.

Dimaag mein lagbhag 86 billion neurons hote hain, jo synapses se jude hote hain. 1943 ke paper ne kaha ki neuron ek tarah se AND / OR / NOT logic karta hai — matlab dimaag ko ek computing machine ki tarah samjha ja sakta hai.

Yeh idea hi baad mein Artificial Neural Networks ki neev bana — computer mein dimaag jaisi structure banana.

Lekin dimaag sirf logic nahi hai. Woh analogue hai, emotions aur memory se bhara hai — aur aaj bhi scientists poori tarah nahi samajh paye ki woh kaise kaam karta hai.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 1

1.5Chapter 1 — AI Foundations

Cybernetics — feedback loop ka idea (1948)

1948 mein ek kitab "Cybernetics: Or Control and Communication in the Animal and the Machine" aayi. Isne feedback loop ka idea diya — machine apne action ka result dekh kar khud ko sudhaare.

Feedback loop ka matlab: machine kuch karti hai, result measure karti hai, aur agar result galat hai to apna action badal leti hai. Jaise thermostat — garmi badhe to AC chalu, thand badhe to band.

Yeh kitab bestseller bani. Isne pehle se hi bhavishyavani ki thi ki machines ek din chess mein insaan ko hara dengi — aur yeh 1997 mein sach hua.

Lekin kitab ne chetavani bhi di thi: agar machines ko bina soche-samjhe use kiya gaya to insaan ka kaam aur zindagi "dehumanize" ho sakti hai — matlab insaaniyat kam ho sakti hai.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 1
← PreviousDimaag ek machine hai? — 1943 ka paperNext →AI ki origin story — Dartmouth 1956
1.6Chapter 1 — AI Foundations

AI ki origin story — Dartmouth 1956

1956 ki garmi mein Dartmouth College mein ek 10-hafte ka project hua — wahi pehli baar "artificial intelligence" shabd use hua.

Usse pehle, Logic Theorist banaya ja chuka tha — pehla AI program. Isne ek mashhoor ganit ki kitab (Principia Mathematica) ke theorems solve kiye. Yeh IBM 701 computer par chala aur iske liye IPL language banayi gayi — list processing ke liye.

1950s ke end mein Lisp language aayi — ismein recursion, dynamic typing aur garbage collection thi. Yeh AI research ki pasandida language ban gayi aur MIT AI Lab ki neev mein iska bada haath tha.

1961 mein time-sharing aaya — ek hi computer ko kai log ek saath use kar sakte the. Yahi idea aage chal kar Internet aur cloud computing bana.

1969 mein "Computer-Controlled Cars" par paper aaya, aur 1971 mein AI ke ek pioneer ko Turing Award mila — computer science ka sabse bada samman.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 1
← PreviousCybernetics — feedback loop ka idea (1948)Next →Golden Age 1956–1974 — ummeedon ka daur
1.7Chapter 1 — AI Foundations

Golden Age 1956–1974 — ummeedon ka daur

1956 se 1974 tak AI ka golden age tha. Vacuum tubes ki jagah integrated circuits aaye, aur Sputnik ke baad America ne ARPA ke through research par bahut paisa lagaya. ARPA ka funda tha — "fund people, not projects", matlab logon par bharosa karo.

Is daur ki mashhoor uplabdhiyan:

  • General Problem Solver (1959) — har tarah ki problem solve karne ki koshish
  • SAINT (1961) — calculus ke sawaal solve karta tha
  • ANALOGY (1963) — analogy wale sawaal
  • STUDENT (1964) — algebra ke word problems samajhta tha
  • ELIZA (1965) — pehla chatbot, ek psychoanalyst ki nakal karta tha
  • Computer Vision (1966) — machine ko dekhna sikhana
  • Mac Hack (1968) — chess khelne wala program, C-rating tak pahuncha
  • Hearsay I — speech recognition ki shuruaat

Isi daur mein do school bane: symbolic AI (rules aur logic se) aur connectionism (neural networks se). Dono ke beech bahas chalti rahi.

1957 mein Mark 1 Perceptron bana — 20×20 pixels dekh kar seekhta tha, weights adjust karke. Newspapers ne bahut hype kar diya. Lekin 1969 mein ek kitab "Perceptrons" ne dikhaya ki iski limits hain — aur neural network research ruk gaya.

Badi-badi bhavishyavaniyan bhi galat nikli: 1965 mein kaha gaya "20 saal mein machine insaan jitni smart hogi", 1970 mein kaha gaya "3–8 saal mein". Dono galat nikle.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 1

1.8Chapter 1 — AI Foundations

AI Winter — jab funding ruk gayi (1970s)

1970s ke shuru mein AI par thand pad gayi — is daur ko AI Winter kehte hain. Funding kati, aur researchers ko apna kaam chhupana pada.

Kaaran kai the:

  • Computer bahut kamzor the — ek mashhoor machine (DEC PDP-11/45) mein sirf 128K memory thi.
  • Disambiguation problem — ek hi shabd ke kai matlab hote hain, machine confuse ho jati thi.
  • 1970s mein inflation aur oil crisis ne budget kata.
  • DARPA ka Speech Understanding project — Harpy system sirf 1,011 shabd samajhta tha (ek 3 saal ke bachche jitna), aur $3M ka budget kat gaya.
  • Lighthill Report (1973) — Britain ki ek report ne kaha ki AI ne "combinatorial explosion" ki wajah se kuch khaas nahi kiya. TV par debate bhi hui. Report ne kaha — "no major impact promised".

Is daur mein researchers ne apne kaam ko "machine learning" ya "pattern recognition" kehna shuru kar diya — taaki "AI" shabd se funding na ruke.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 1
← PreviousGolden Age 1956–1974 — ummeedon ka daurNext →Expert Systems — 1980s ka boom aur phir girawat
1.9Chapter 1 — AI Foundations

Expert Systems — 1980s ka boom aur phir girawat

AI Winter ke beech hi do cheezein invent hui jo baad mein kaam aayi — backpropagation aur Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN). Lekin 1980s mein ek nayi leher aayi: Expert Systems.

Expert System ka matlab: human expert ke rules ko computer mein daal do — If-Then rules. Jaise "agar patient ko bukhaar hai aur khaansi hai, to flu ho sakta hai".

Sabse mashhoor example tha XCON (1980) — ek computer company ke liye system jo computer configure karta tha. Ismein lagbhag 2,500 rules the, aur 1986 tak isne company ko lagbhag $40 million bachaye.

Expert Systems billion-dollar industry ban gayi. 1996 mein Deep Blue ne chess ke grandmaster ko hara diya — 200 million positions per second check karke.

Lekin Expert Systems mein khaamiyan thi:

  • Bahut narrow — sirf ek hi kaam kar sakte the.
  • Maintain karna mushkil — har naya rule likhna padta tha.
  • Experts aapas mein disagree karte the — kis ka rule sahi hai?
  • Yeh seekhte nahi the — naya data aaye to bhi wahi purane rules.

Isi liye 1990s ke aas-paas doosra AI Winter aaya, jo lagbhag 1993 tak chala.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 1

1.10Chapter 1 — AI Foundations

Neural Networks ki wapsi — 1986 ke baad

1986 mein ek paper "Learning Representations by Back-propagating Errors" aaya — isne neural networks ko dobara zinda kar diya.

Is daur ki key milestones:

  • 1980 — Neocognitron: yeh baad mein CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) ki neev bana.
  • 1982 — Hopfield Networks: memory jaisa kaam karne wala network.
  • 1989: ek researcher ne CNN + backprop se handwritten cheques padhna sikhaya.
  • 1989 — Q-Learning thesis: reinforcement learning ki neev.
  • 1998: gradient-based document recognition — machine documents padhne lagi.

Backpropagation ka idea simple hai: network galti kare to us galti ko peeche bhej kar weights ko sudhaaro — baar-baar, jab tak galti kam na ho jaye.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 1

1.11Chapter 1 — AI Foundations

AI ke drivers — data, cloud aur GPUs

2010 ke baad AI achanak itni tez kyun badhi? Teen drivers the — data, computing power aur algorithms.

1. Explosive datasets: Internet, smartphones aur social media se data ka samundar ban gaya. Machine learning ko seekhne ke liye bahut saara data chahiye — aur woh milne laga.

2. Google infrastructure: commodity clusters (saste computers ko jod kar supercomputer banana), virtualization aur open source ne computing sasti kar di. 2011 mein Google Brain bana — deep learning par bada project.

3. GPUs: NVIDIA ke GPUs (jo pehle games ke liye bane the) ne parallel processing di. Jo kaam pehle hafton-mahinon mein hota tha, woh dinon mein hone laga.

In teeno ne mil kar deep learning ko aisi taakat di jo pehle kabhi nahi thi.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 1
← PreviousNeural Networks ki wapsi — 1986 ke baadNext →AI ki structure — ML aur Deep Learning kahan aate hain?
1.12Chapter 1 — AI Foundations

AI ki structure — ML aur Deep Learning kahan aate hain?

AI ek bada umbrella hai. Uske andar Machine Learning aata hai, aur uske andar Deep Learning. Yeh teenon ek ke andar ek hain.

  • Artificial Intelligence (AI) — sabse bada circle: computer ko intelligent banane ki koshish.
  • Machine Learning (ML) — AI ka hissa: computer data se seekhe, bina har rule likhe.
  • Deep Learning (DL) — ML ka hissa: neural networks jismein kai layers hoti hain.

Chapter 1 ke Key Takeaways: Weak AI aaj ki haqeeqat hai, Strong AI abhi sapna hai. Turing Test intelligent hone ki kasauti hai. AI ka itihaas upar-neeche raha — Golden Age, AI Winter, Expert Systems, phir Neural Networks ki wapsi. Aaj AI ki taakat ke peeche data, cloud aur GPUs hain.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 1

2.1Chapter 2 — Data

Data kyun sabse important hai

AI ka pehla rule: garbage in, garbage out. Agar data kharab hai to model kitna bhi achha ho, result kharab hi hoga. Isi liye data AI ka sabse important hissa hai.

Pinterest ka case: ek baar Pinterest ne ek user ko shaadi se judi emails bhejni shuru kar di — lekin user ki shaadi tooti hui thi. Company ke 250 million monthly users aur $756 million revenue (2018) ke bawajood, yeh galti hui. Company ko maafi maangni padi — "overbearing mother" jaisa behave karne ke liye.

Target ka case: ek retail chain ne ek ladki ko pregnancy se judi cheezein bhej di — uske pita naraaz ho gaye. Baad mein pata chala ki ladki sach mein pregnant thi — model ko pita se pehle pata chal gaya tha! Yeh dikhata hai ki data se kitni gehri baat pata chal sakti hai.

Is chapter mein hum data ko gehrai se samjhenge — types, Big Data, databases, aur data ko AI ke liye taiyaar karne ka process.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 2
← PreviousAI ki structure — ML aur Deep Learning kahan aate hain?Next →Data basics — bit, byte aur Table 2-1
2.2Chapter 2 — Data

Data basics — bit, byte aur Table 2-1

Data ki sabse chhoti unit hai bit — 0 ya 1. 8 bits mil kar ek byte banta hai. Uske baad units badi hoti jati hain.

UnitSizeKitna data?
Kilobyte (KB)1,000 bytesEk chhota text page
Megabyte (MB)1,000 KBEk chhoti kitab
Gigabyte (GB)1,000 MBLagbhag 230 gaane
Terabyte (TB)1,000 GB500 ghante ki filmein
Petabyte (PB)1,000 TB5 saal ke EOS (Earth Observing System) data
Exabyte (EB)1,000 PBLibrary of Congress ka 3,000 guna
Zettabyte (ZB)1,000 EB36,000 saal ki HD-TV
Yottabyte (YB)1,000 ZBDelaware + Rhode Island jitna bada data center

Table 2-1: Data ki units — kitab ke hisaab se poori list. Note karo: yahan 1,000 ka hisaab use hua hai (decimal), 1,024 ka nahi.

Data kahan se aata hai? Web aur social media, biometrics (chehra, ungli ke nishaan), POS (point of sale — dukaan par payment), IoT devices (sensors), cloud aur corporate databases/spreadsheets.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 2

2.3Chapter 2 — Data

Data ke types — structured, unstructured, semi-structured

Har data ek jaisa nahi hota. AI project mein pehle ye samajhna hota hai ki data kis type ka hai.

Structured data (lagbhag 20%): jo table mein fit ho — rows aur columns. Jaise CRM/ERP systems ka data, spreadsheets. Ise BI (Business Intelligence) tools se aasani se analyse kar sakte ho.

Unstructured data (sabse zyada): jo table mein fit na ho — images, video, audio, text, social media posts, satellite images. Ise handle karne ke liye NoSQL databases chahiye.

Semi-structured data (5–10%): beech ka — jaise XML aur JSON, jo APIs se milte hain. Ismein kuch structure hota hai, lekin poora table nahi banta.

Time-series data: jo waqt ke saath badle — jaise customer journey, sensor readings. Yeh messy hota hai: trillions of points, aur intent samajhna mushkil hota hai.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 2
← PreviousData basics — bit, byte aur Table 2-1Next →Big Data — 3 Vs aur badi-badi numbers
2.4Chapter 2 — Data

Big Data — 3 Vs aur badi-badi numbers

Big Data ka matlab hai — itna bada data jo normal tools se handle na ho. Iske teen Vs hain, jo 2001 mein ek analyst ne diye the.

Paimaane dekho: Google par har second 40,000 searches hoti hain — din mein 3.5 billion. Snapchat par har minute 527,760 photos. YouTube par har minute 4.1 million videos dekhe jate hain. Har minute 156 million emails bheje jate hain. 2020 tak 12.86 billion sensors hone ka estimate tha.

IDC ke "Data Age 2025" report ke hisaab se 2025 tak duniya mein 163 Zettabytes data hoga — 2017 se 10 guna zyada.

Teen Vs:

  • Volume — kitna data hai: tens of Terabytes. Cloud aur NoSQL se handle hota hai.
  • Variety — kitne types ka data hai: text, image, video, sensor — sab mila hua.
  • Velocity — kitni tez data aa raha hai: firehose ki tarah. In-memory processing chahiye. Yeh sabse mushkil V hai.

Baad mein aur Vs bhi jode gaye — Veracity (data kitna sachha hai), Value (data se kya value milegi), Variability (data kitna badalta hai), Visualization (data ko dikhana). Aaj 10 se zyada Vs gine jate hain.

Ek badi database company ne kaha tha: "big data has become capital" — matlab data ab paise jaisi asset hai.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 2
← PreviousData ke types — structured, unstructured, semi-structuredNext →Databases aur tools — SQL se Hadoop tak
2.5Chapter 2 — Data

Databases aur tools — SQL se Hadoop tak

Data ko store aur process karne ke liye alag-alag tools bane hain. Har tool ka apna kaam hai.

Relational Database (1970): ek researcher ne "A Relational Model of Data for Large Shared Data Banks" paper likha. Ismein data tables mein hota hai, SQL language se CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) karte hain. Primary key aur foreign key se tables judte hain. Relationships teen tarah ke: One-to-One, One-to-Many, Many-to-Many.

Ek badi company ne is paper ko padh kar 1977 mein apni database company shuru ki. IBM ka DB2 1993 mein aaya — lekin der ho chuki thi.

Relational databases ki khaamiyan: data sprawl (data har jagah bikhra), naye environments mein mushkil, high costs, development challenges.

Lucene (late 1990s): text search ke liye.

Hadoop: Google ke file-system paper (2003) aur MapReduce par based. Pehle Yahoo! phir Facebook/Twitter ne use kiya. Isse poora 360° view milta hai. Hortonworks ne YARN diya. Storm/Spark streaming ke liye (real-time), Hadoop batch ke liye.

MongoDB: document model, petabyte scale, 40 million+ downloads, Oct 2017 mein IPO.

Data Lake: data ko bina reformat kiye store karo — structured bhi, unstructured bhi. Ek study ke hisaab se data lake use karne wali companies ki organic growth 9% zyada thi. Data Warehouse sirf structured data ke liye hota hai; Data Lake har tarah ke data ke liye.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 2
← PreviousBig Data — 3 Vs aur badi-badi numbersNext →Data process — CRISP-DM aur 80% waala rule
2.6Chapter 2 — Data

Data process — CRISP-DM aur 80% waala rule

Data ko AI ke liye taiyaar karna hi sabse bada kaam hai. Pehle 3 steps mein hi 80% waqt lag jata hai.

Pehle numbers: IDC ke hisaab se Big Data par kharcha $166 billion (2018) se badh kar $260 billion (2022) hone ka estimate tha — 11.9% CAGR. Lekin Gartner ke hisaab se lagbhag 85% Big Data projects pilot se pehle hi fail ho jate hain. Kaaran: clear focus nahi, ganda data, galat tools, collection problems, stakeholder buy-in nahi.

CRISP-DM (late 1990s) data process ka standard framework hai — iterative hai, linear nahi. Matlab steps ko baar-baar dohraya jata hai.

CRISP-DM ke 6 steps hain: (1) Business Understanding, (2) Data Understanding, (3) Data Preparation, (4) Modelling, (5) Evaluation, (6) Deployment. Pehle 3 steps mein 80% waqt lagta hai — aur wahi is chapter ke agle sections mein hain.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 2
← PreviousDatabases aur tools — SQL se Hadoop takNext →Step 1 — Business Understanding
2.7Chapter 2 — Data

Step 1 — Business Understanding

AI project shuru karne se pehle yeh tay karo: success ka matlab kya hai? Sales +1%? Conversions +5%? Bina clear goal ke AI project bhatak jata hai.

AB InBev ka case: ek badi beer company ne packaging line ki motors par 20 wireless vibration sensors lagaye. Sensor ne anomaly (gadbad) detect ki — machine kharab hone se pehle hi pata chal gaya. Predictive maintenance ka perfect example.

Moneyball: ek baseball team ne data se team banayi — batting average ki jagah slugging percentage aur on-base percentage ko importance di. Kam budget mein badi team ko takkar di.

Team mein kya chahiye: kuch data scientists + domain experts (jo business samajhte hon) + infrastructure ki evaluation. Sirf data scientists se kaam nahi chalega.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 2
← PreviousData process — CRISP-DM aur 80% waala ruleNext →Step 2 — Data Understanding
2.8Chapter 2 — Data

Step 2 — Data Understanding

Data kahan se aayega? Aam taur par: in-house data lagbhag 70%, open source lagbhag 20%, baaki third-party se.

Data ko evaluate karne ke sawaal:

  • Data complete hai ya gaps hain?
  • Data kahan se aaya (provenance)?
  • Data kahan-kahan collect hua?
  • Data ko kis-kis ne chhua (touch) hai?
  • Data mein kya changes hue hain?
  • Data ki quality kaisi hai?

Unstructured data ke liye labelling badi mushkil hai — har image/video ko label karna padta hai, jo bahut mehnat ka kaam hai.

Yaad rakho: "garbage in, garbage out" — ganda data daaloge to ganda result milega.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 2
← PreviousStep 1 — Business UnderstandingNext →Step 3 — Data Preparation (sabse lamba kaam)
2.9Chapter 2 — Data

Step 3 — Data Preparation (sabse lamba kaam)

Data ko saaf karna aur model ke layak banana — yahi Data Preparation hai. Ismein sabse zyada waqt lagta hai.

Mortgage crisis ka sabak: models ne yeh miss kar diya ki ghar ke daam gir sakte hain — result $700 billion ka bailout. Data mein woh scenario hi nahi tha.

Cleansing mein kya-kya hota hai:

  • De-duplication — duplicate records hatana
  • Outliers — bahut alag values ko handle karna
  • Consistency — ek hi cheez ke alag-alag format ko ek karna
  • Validation rules — jaise age > 120 ho to flag karo
  • Binning — data ko groups mein baantna
  • Staleness — purana data hatana
  • Merging — alag sources ka data jodna
  • One-hot encoding — categorical data ko numbers mein badalna. Jaise Apple/Pineapple/Orange → teen columns: is_Apple, is_Pineapple, is_Orange (0 ya 1)

Tools: SAS, Oracle, IBM, Lavastorm, Talend (commercial); OpenRefine, plyr, reshape2 (open source).

BlueVine ka case: ek fintech company ne customer ki websites ko scrape karke pata lagaya ki business kis type ka hai — isse lending decisions behtar hui.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 2
← PreviousStep 2 — Data UnderstandingNext →Ethics aur Governance — data ka galat istemal
2.10Chapter 2 — Data

Ethics aur Governance — data ka galat istemal

Data powerful hai — aur galat haathon mein khatarnak bhi. Isi liye ethics aur governance zaroori hai.

Cambridge Analytica: Facebook ka data political profiling ke liye use hua. Facebook ki value $100 billion se zyada gir gayi.

Scraping ka legal risk: kisi ki website se data uthana legal trouble mein daal sakta hai.

MIT study: anonymized data bhi safe nahi — Singapore ke mobile + transport data se 11 hafte mein 95% logon ko dobara pehchan liya gaya.

Verizon 2018 report: 53,000+ incidents, lagbhag 2,200 breaches. 76% financially motivated, 73% external attackers, lagbhag aadhe organized crime, 12% nation-state.

Isi liye har AI project mein legal department ko shuru se involve karo. Data governance ka matlab hai — kaun sa data, kis ke liye, kis tarah use hoga, yeh pehle se tay ho.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 2
← PreviousStep 3 — Data Preparation (sabse lamba kaam)Next →Kitna data chahiye? — Hughes Phenomenon
2.11Chapter 2 — Data

Kitna data chahiye? — Hughes Phenomenon

Zyada data hamesha behtar nahi hota. Kabhi-kabhi zyada features se problem badh jati hai — isse Hughes Phenomenon ya curse of dimensionality kehte hain.

Curse of dimensionality ka matlab: jaise-jaise features (columns) badhte hain, utna hi zyada data chahiye hota hai — exponential tareeke se. Ek RGB image mein hi lagbhag 7,500 dimensions hote hain (har pixel ke 3 colour values)!

Isi liye feature selection important hai — sirf wahi features rakho jo kaam ke hain. Baaki ko hata do.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 2
← PreviousEthics aur Governance — data ka galat istemalNext →Data ke important terms — ek jhalak mein
2.12Chapter 2 — Data

Data ke important terms — ek jhalak mein

Data ki duniya mein kai terms baar-baar aayenge. Yeh raha unka quick reference:

TermMatlab
CategoricalText wala data, jaise gender ya category
Data TypeVariable kis type ki hai — Boolean, integer, string, floating point
Descriptive AnalyticsKya hua? (past ko samajhna)
Diagnostic AnalyticsKyun hua? (reason dhoondhna)
Predictive AnalyticsKya hoga? (future predict karna)
Prescriptive AnalyticsKya karna chahiye? (action batana)
ETLExtract, Transform, Load — data ko warehouse mein daalne ka process
FeatureData ka ek column
InstanceData ki ek row
MetadataData ke baare mein data — jaise file ka size, date, genre
Numerical (discrete vs continuous)Discrete = ginne wala (1, 2, 3); Continuous = measure wala (1.5, 2.7)
OLAPOnline Analytical Processing — data ko alag angles se analyse karna
OrdinalOrder wala data, jaise 5-star rating
Scalar VariablesEk hi value wali variable
Transactional DataHar transaction ka record, jaise kharidari

Chapter 2 ke Key Takeaways: Data AI ki neev hai — "garbage in, garbage out". Structured data sirf 20% hai; baaki unstructured ya semi-structured hai. Big Data ke 3 Vs hain — Volume, Variety, Velocity. CRISP-DM process mein pehle 3 steps mein 80% waqt lagta hai. Data ki ethics aur governance ko halke mein mat lo.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 2
← PreviousKitna data chahiye? — Hughes PhenomenonNext →Machine Learning kya hai — Stitch Fix ki kahani
3.1Chapter 3 — Machine Learning

Machine Learning kya hai — Stitch Fix ki kahani

Machine Learning ka matlab hai — computer data se seekhe, bina har rule likhe. 1959 mein ek paper mein ek checkers khelne wale program se yeh dikhaya gaya tha: machine "learn without being explicitly programmed" kar sakti hai.

Stitch Fix ki kahani: ek founder ne 2011 mein apne Cambridge apartment se ek company shuru ki — pehla naam "Rack Habit" tha. Customer ek Q&A bharta tha, stylist kapde chun kar monthly box bhejta tha.

Company ne ek badi streaming company ke ex-data-science VP ko chief algorithms officer banaya. 2017 mein unhone apna private label "Hybrid Designs" launch kiya. Nov 2017 mein IPO hua — $120 million raise, $1.63 billion valuation. 2.7 million customers, $1.2 billion se zyada revenue, 100+ data scientists (zyadatar PhD).

Company ki 10-K filing mein likha tha ki data science hi styling, prediction, inventory aur design ko chalata hai. Yeh ML ki taakat hai — data se faisle, guess se nahi.

Ek mashhoor example: "hot dog / not hot dog" — labelled data do, machine seekh legi ki photo mein hot dog hai ya nahi. Labels hi ML ki neev hain.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 3
← PreviousData ke important terms — ek jhalak meinNext →Statistics ki neev — Standard Deviation aur Normal Distribution
3.2Chapter 3 — Machine Learning

Statistics ki neev — Standard Deviation aur Normal Distribution

ML samajhne ke liye thodi statistics zaroori hai. Do concepts sabse important hain — Standard Deviation aur Normal Distribution.

Standard Deviation (SD)

SD batata hai ki data mean (average) se kitna door bikhra hai. Example: ghar ki keemat ka mean $145,000 hai aur SD $24,000 hai — matlab zyadatar ghar $133,000 se $157,000 ke beech hain.

Agar ek bahut mehenga ghar (outlier) aa jaye to mean $850,000 ho jata hai aur SD $175,000 — isliye outlier ko alag karna padta hai, warna average bigad jata hai.

Normal Distribution (Bell Curve)

Jab data ko plot karo to ghanti (bell) jaisi shape banti hai — beech mein zyada, kinare par kam. Iska rule hai 68-95-99.7: 68% data mean ± 1 SD mein, 95% mean ± 2 SD mein, 99.7% mean ± 3 SD mein hota hai.

IQ ka example: mean 100, SD 15. IQ 145 wala insaan sirf 0.15% logon se upar hai. Kabhi-kabhi curve ek taraf jhuk jata hai — isse skew kehte hain.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 3
← PreviousMachine Learning kya hai — Stitch Fix ki kahaniNext →Bayes' Theorem — probability ko sudhaarna
3.3Chapter 3 — Machine Learning

Bayes' Theorem — probability ko sudhaarna

Bayes' Theorem ek formula hai jo nayi jaankari milne par probability ko update karta hai. ML mein yeh bahut kaam aata hai.

Cancer test ka worked example: ek test 80% baar sahi positive deta hai (true positive rate 80%), aur 9.6% baar galat positive deta hai (false positive rate). Bimari sirf 1% logon mein hai. Agar aapka test positive aaya, to aapko sach mein bimari hone ki probability kitni hai?

Zyadatar log kahenge 80%. Lekin sahi jawab hai sirf 7.8%! Kyunki bimari bahut rare hai, isliye zyadatar positive results false positive hote hain.

Calculation 3 steps mein:

  • Step 1: P(bimari aur positive) = 0.01 × 0.80 = 0.008
  • Step 2: P(positive) = 0.008 + (0.99 × 0.096) = 0.008 + 0.09504 = 0.10304
  • Step 3: P(bimari | positive) = 0.008 / 0.10304 = 7.8%

Yahi Bayes' Theorem hai — base rate (kitne logon mein bimari hai) ko bhoolna sabse badi galti hai. ML models mein bhi yahi galti hoti hai.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 3
← PreviousStatistics ki neev — Standard Deviation aur Normal DistributionNext →Correlation — aur 'correlation ≠ causation'
3.4Chapter 3 — Machine Learning

Correlation — aur 'correlation ≠ causation'

Correlation batata hai ki do cheezein kitni saath chalti hain. Pearson correlation -1 se +1 ke beech hota hai.

Example: income aur spending ka correlation 0.9 hai — matlab income $1,000 badhe to spending lagbhag $900 badhti hai. +0.7 se upar strong correlation, +0.3 se neeche tenuous (kamzor) mana jata hai.

Lekin yaad rakho: "correlation does not imply causation" — do cheezein saath badh rahi hain, iska matlab yeh nahi ki ek ne doosri ko cause kiya.

Spurious correlations (bewakoof wale examples):

  • Ek state mein divorce rate aur margarine ki khapat ka correlation 99.26%!
  • Ek beauty pageant winner ki umar aur steam se hone wali mauton ka correlation 87.01%!
  • Ek desh ke oil imports aur train se hone wali mauton ka correlation 95.4%!

Insaan ka dimaag patterns dhoondhta hai — isse patternicity kehte hain. ML model bhi aise hi galat patterns seekh sakta hai, isliye correlation ko hamesha test karo.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 3
← PreviousBayes' Theorem — probability ko sudhaarnaNext →Feature Extraction — machine ko kya dikhana hai
3.5Chapter 3 — Machine Learning

Feature Extraction — machine ko kya dikhana hai

Feature Extraction ka matlab hai — data mein se woh variables chunna jo model ke liye kaam ki hain. Galat features chunoge to model galat seekhega.

Example: male vs female face pehchanne ke liye features:

FeatureMaleFemale
EyebrowsThicker, straighterThinner, arched
FaceLonger, larger, squareRounder, smaller
JawboneSquare, wider, sharperRounder, narrower
NeckAdam's apple dikhta haiAdam's apple nahi dikhta

Table 3-1: Face ke features — male vs female. Yeh features model ko sikhane ke liye use hote hain.

Ek aur baat: features mein bias chhup sakta hai. Agar training data mein ek hi type ke chehre zyada hain, to model doosre chehron par galat hoga.

Deep Learning ki khaasiyat yahi hai — woh features khud dhoondh leta hai, insaan ko batane ki zaroorat nahi padti.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 3
← PreviousCorrelation — aur 'correlation ≠ causation'Next →ML se kya-kya kar sakte ho — real use cases
3.6Chapter 3 — Machine Learning

ML se kya-kya kar sakte ho — real use cases

ML har industry mein ghus chuka hai. Kuch real examples dekhte hain:

  • Predictive maintenance: ek drone company ne inspection ki keemat $80–90 se ghata kar $45–60 per well pad kar di — lagbhag 66% saving.
  • Recruiting: ek hiring platform ke paas 2.3 million jobs, 680 million profiles, 310 million resumes, 10 million titles, 1.3 billion skills aur 2.5 million background checks ka data hai. Ek hire ke liye sirf 75 applications lagti hain, industry average lagbhag 150 hai.
  • Customer experience: ek grocery chain ne 60 million+ households ka data analyse kiya — avocado 4-packs ne Millennials ko attract kiya, sales badhi.
  • Finance aur RPA: fraud detection, loan approvals.
  • Customer service: chatbots.
  • Dating: ek dating app roz 10 billion se zyada photos ko label karti hai.
SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 3
← PreviousFeature Extraction — machine ko kya dikhana haiNext →ML process — 5 steps, train/test split
3.7Chapter 3 — Machine Learning

ML process — 5 steps, train/test split

ML model banana ek process hai — 5 steps. Sabse pehle data ko visualize karo, phir model banao.

Step 1 — Data Order: data ko randomize karo. Agar data sorted hai (jaise saare positive pehle, negative baad mein) to model galat seekhega.

Step 2 — Choose a Model: educated guess se model chuno, trial and error se. Koi ek model har problem ke liye best nahi hota.

Step 3 — Train: lagbhag 70% data se model ko train karo. Used-car example: price = m × (kuch) + b — yahan m slope hai, b intercept hai. Inhe weights kehte hain.

Step 4 — Evaluate: baaki 30% test data se check karo. Train aur test data ko kabhi mix mat karo — yeh sabse common galti hai. Accuracy kabhi-kabhi dhokha deti hai — fraud example mein 99% accuracy bhi bekaar ho sakti hai agar fraud sirf 1% hai. Bayes bhi use karo.

Step 5 — Fine-Tune: parameters aur hyperparameters ko adjust karo. Hyperparameters woh settings hain jo training se nahi seekhi jati — jaise learning rate.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 3
← PreviousML se kya-kya kar sakte ho — real use casesNext →Supervised Learning — labelled data se seekhna
3.8Chapter 3 — Machine Learning

Supervised Learning — labelled data se seekhna

Supervised Learning mein machine ko labelled data diya jata hai — har example ke saath sahi jawab likha hota hai. Jaise dog-breed wali photos, har photo par breed ka naam likha ho.

Iske liye bahut saara data chahiye, aur labelling mein bahut mehnat lagti hai. ImageNet banane mein crowdsourcing se saalon lag gaye.

Ek badi social media company ne 2018 mein 3.5 billion Instagram photos use ki — hashtags ko labels ki tarah use kiya. Isse "weakly supervised" learning kehte hain. Result: ImageNet benchmark par 85.4% accuracy — sabse zyada, pichle record se 2% upar. Ismein 336 GPUs aur ek model use hua jismein 861 million+ parameters the.

Uses: newsfeed ranking, objectionable content hatana, visually impaired logon ke liye auto-captions.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 3
← PreviousML process — 5 steps, train/test splitNext →Unsupervised Learning — bina labels ke patterns
3.9Chapter 3 — Machine Learning

Unsupervised Learning — bina labels ke patterns

Unsupervised Learning mein data par koi label nahi hota — machine khud patterns dhoondhti hai. Isse clustering kehte hain.

Distance measure karne ke tareeke: Euclidean (seedha distance), Cosine Similarity (angle), Manhattan (grid wala distance).

Uses:

  • Customer segmentation — customers ko groups mein baantna
  • Sentiment analysis — log kya feel kar rahe hain
  • Association — "agar X to Y" — jaise "jo yeh khareedta hai, woh woh bhi khareedta hai" (recommendation engines)
  • Anomaly Detection — jo normal se alag hai use pakdo, jaise email security mein spam
  • Autoencoders — data ko compress karke dobara banao; noise hatane mein kaam aata hai

Teen mashhoor researchers ne ek Nature paper mein likha tha ki unsupervised learning aage chal kar supervised se bhi zyada important ho jayegi — kyunki duniya mein zyadatar data bina labels ke hai.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 3
← PreviousSupervised Learning — labelled data se seekhnaNext →Reinforcement Learning — reward aur punishment se
3.10Chapter 3 — Machine Learning

Reinforcement Learning — reward aur punishment se

Reinforcement Learning mein machine trial-and-error se seekhti hai — sahi kaam par reward, galat par punishment.

Games mein yeh bahut kaam aata hai — Go aur chess mein machine ne lakhon simulations khel kar seekha. Robotics mein bhi — navigation, kitchen mein kaam karna.

Iska idea simple hai: machine action leti hai, environment se feedback milta hai, aur woh apni strategy sudhaarti hai. Jaise bachcha chalna seekhta hai — girta hai, uthta hai, phir chalta hai.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 3
← PreviousUnsupervised Learning — bina labels ke patternsNext →Semi-supervised Learning — thoda label, bahut data
3.11Chapter 3 — Machine Learning

Semi-supervised Learning — thoda label, bahut data

Semi-supervised Learning beech ka rasta hai — thoda sa labelled data + bahut saara unlabeled data.

Technique: pseudo-labeling — pehle chhote labelled data se model train karo, phir us model se unlabeled data ko label karo, phir dobara train karo.

Use case: MRI interpretation — labelled MRI scans bahut kam milte hain (doctor ko har scan label karna padta hai), lekin unlabeled scans bahut hain. Semi-supervised se dono ka fayda milta hai.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 3
← PreviousReinforcement Learning — reward aur punishment seNext →Common algorithms — framework ek nazar mein
3.12Chapter 3 — Machine Learning

Common algorithms — framework ek nazar mein

ML ke algorithms ko 2 bade groups mein baanta jata hai — classification aur regression. Neeche framework dekho:

  • Classification: jawab categories mein — jaise spam ya not-spam, dog ya cat.
  • Regression: jawab number mein — jaise ghar ki keemat, temperature.

Agle sections mein 6 mashhoor algorithms detail mein hain — Naïve Bayes, K-Nearest Neighbor, Linear Regression, Decision Tree, Ensemble aur K-Means.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 3
← PreviousSemi-supervised Learning — thoda label, bahut dataNext →Naïve Bayes Classifier — worked example ke saath
3.13Chapter 3 — Machine Learning

Naïve Bayes Classifier — worked example ke saath

Naïve Bayes mein variables ko independent mana jata hai — isi liye "naïve" (bhola) kaha jata hai. Yeh assumption aksar galat hoti hai, lekin phir bhi algorithm bahut achha kaam karta hai.

Variants: Bernoulli, Multinomial, Gaussian. Uses: spam detection, customer segmentation, sentiment analysis, medical diagnosis, weather prediction.

Worked example — e-commerce: kya customer khareedega? Do factors hain — discount mila ya nahi, aur review achha tha ya kharab.

DiscountReviewPurchase?
YesHighYes
NoLowNo
YesLowYes
NoHighNo

Tables 3-2 to 3-5: dataset, frequency table aur probability table — kitab mein poora calculation diya hai. Final result: P(purchase | low review) = 7/24 = 29%.

Matlab: agar review low hai to khareedne ki probability sirf 29% hai. Yeh calculation Bayes' Theorem par based hai — pehle prior probability, phir likelihood, phir posterior.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 3
← PreviousCommon algorithms — framework ek nazar meinNext →K-Nearest Neighbor (k-NN) — 'birds of a feather'
3.14Chapter 3 — Machine Learning

K-Nearest Neighbor (k-NN) — 'birds of a feather'

k-NN ka funda hai — "birds of a feather flock together", matlab jo paas hain woh ek jaise hote hain. Naye data point ko dekho, uske k nearest neighbours dekho, aur majority ki category de do.

Use case: credit score — naye applicant ke sabse kareebi (similar) purane applicants dekho, unka behaviour dekh kar faisla karo.

Isse "lazy learning" kehte hain — kyunki ismein training hoti hi nahi, prediction ke waqt hi calculation hota hai.

Distance kaise measure karein? Numbers ke liye Euclidean distance, categories ke liye overlap metric.

k kitna rakhein? Zyada neighbours = smoother result, lekin cost zyada. Kareeb wale data ko zyada weight dena behtar hota hai.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 3
← PreviousNaïve Bayes Classifier — worked example ke saathNext →Linear Regression — worked example aur R-squared
3.15Chapter 3 — Machine Learning

Linear Regression — worked example aur R-squared

Linear Regression do variables ke beech seedhi line wala rishta dhoondhta hai. Example: padhai ke ghante vs grade.

Study HoursGrade
10.69
20.76
30.80
40.84
50.87
60.91
70.95

Table 3-6: 12 data points (1–7 ghante). Kitab mein poori table di hai.

Least squares method se best-fit line nikali jati hai — woh line jo saare points se sabse kam door ho.

Equation: Grade = hours × 0.03731 + 0.6889. 4 ghante padho to grade = 0.838.

R-squared = 0.9180 — matlab padhai ke ghante grade ke 91.8% variation ko samjhate hain. R-squared 0 se 1 ke beech hota hai; 1 ke kareeb ho to model behtar hai.

Aur types: Multivariate regression (ek se zyada variables) aur Polynomial regression (non-linear rishta, curve wali line).

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 3
← PreviousK-Nearest Neighbor (k-NN) — 'birds of a feather'Next →Decision Tree — Titanic example
3.16Chapter 3 — Machine Learning

Decision Tree — Titanic example

Decision Tree ek flowchart jaisa hota hai — root node se shuru, har node par ek sawaal, aakhir mein leaf par faisla.

Titanic survival example: pehla sawaal — sex? Phir age? Phir sibsp (saath mein kitne bhai-behen)? Har answer ke hisaab se aage badho, aakhir mein pata chalega ki vyakti bacha ya nahi.

Pros: samajhna aasan, bade datasets par chal jata hai, transparent hai — har faisla dikhta hai.

Cons: galti aage badhti hai (ek galat split poora tree bigaad deta hai), aur tree bada hone par complexity aur performance issues aate hain.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 3
← PreviousLinear Regression — worked example aur R-squaredNext →Ensemble Modelling — Netflix Prize ki kahani
3.17Chapter 3 — Machine Learning

Ensemble Modelling — Netflix Prize ki kahani

Ensemble Modelling ka matlab — ek model ki jagah kai models use karo, aur unka combined result lo. Kai baar yeh ek model se behtar hota hai.

Netflix Prize (2006): Netflix ne $1 million ka inaam rakha — jo bhi unke recommendation system ki accuracy 10% se zyada badha de. Data: 100 million+ ratings, 17,770 movies, 480,189 users. 30,000+ teams ne download kiya.

2009 mein BellKor's Pragmatic Chaos team jeeti. Lekin Netflix ne winning model ko use hi nahi kiya — woh bahut complex tha!

Ensemble ke 2 tareeke:

  • Boosting: models ek ke baad ek bante hain, har naya model pichle ki galtiyan sudhaarta hai (weights adjust karke).
  • Bagging: models parallel bante hain, aakhir mein best ko chuna jata hai.
SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 3
← PreviousDecision Tree — Titanic exampleNext →K-Means Clustering — step by step
3.18Chapter 3 — Machine Learning

K-Means Clustering — step by step

K-Means unlabeled data ko k groups mein baantta hai. Process simple hai: k chuno, centroids rakho, iterate karo jab tak converge na ho jaye.

Steps:

  • Data points ko plot karo. (Figure 3-6)
  • 2 random centroids rakho. (Figure 3-7)
  • Har point ko apne sabse kareebi centroid se jodo, phir centroid ko group ka midpoint banao. Baar-baar dohrayo jab tak centroids hilna band na kar dein — isse convergence kehte hain. (Figure 3-8)
  • Sahi k kaise chunein? Elbow method — jahan curve mude, wahi optimal k hai. (Figure 3-9)

K-Means ki limits:

  • Non-spherical (gole nahi) data par fail hota hai. (Figure 3-10)
  • Thin-data clusters (jahan data bahut kam ho) par fail hota hai. (Figure 3-11)

Alternative: DBScan — lekin ismein bahut compute power chahiye.

Chapter 3 ke Key Takeaways (kitab se): Data scientist ka kaam curiosity-driven hota hai — chhote experiments, poora data access, "full-stack data scientists", aur culture jo "learning by doing" ko badhava de. ML ke 4 types hain — supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement, semi-supervised. Algorithms mein Naïve Bayes, k-NN, Linear Regression, Decision Tree, Ensemble aur K-Means aate hain.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 3
← PreviousEnsemble Modelling — Netflix Prize ki kahaniNext →Deep Learning kya hai — ImageNet ki kahani
4.1Chapter 4 — Deep Learning

Deep Learning kya hai — ImageNet ki kahani

Deep Learning Machine Learning ka woh hissa hai jo neural networks use karta hai — kai layers wale. Iski kahani ImageNet se shuru hoti hai.

Ek researcher ne 3.2 million images aur 5,200+ categories ka dataset banaya — Mechanical Turk par crowdsourcing se (2010 tak). 2012 ke contest mein AlexNet ne 10.8% ke margin se jeeta.

Aaj image recognition ki error rate lagbhag 2% hai — insaan se bhi behtar!

"Deep" ka matlab hai — hidden layers ki sankhya zyada. Jitni zyada layers, utna "deep" network.

Ek mashhoor quote hai: "AI is the new electricity" — matlab AI har industry ko waise hi badal degi jaise bijli ne badla tha. Google Search ne DL ko sirf 2015 se use karna shuru kiya tha — phir bhi isne sab badal diya.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 4
← PreviousK-Means Clustering — step by stepNext →ML vs DL ka farak — ghoda pehchanna
4.2Chapter 4 — Deep Learning

ML vs DL ka farak — ghoda pehchanna

ML aur DL mein sabse bada farak hai feature extraction ka. ML mein insaan ko batana padta hai ki kya dekhna hai; DL khud dhoondh leta hai.

Example — ghoda pehchanne ke liye:

  • ML mein: insaan ko features batane padte hain — shape, hooves (khur), colour, height. Phir model in features se seekhta hai.
  • DL mein: pixels seedha network mein daalo — network khud seekh lega ki ghoda kaisa dikhta hai.

Isi liye DL ko zyada data aur zyada compute chahiye — lekin jab data bahut ho to DL ML se behtar hota hai.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 4
← PreviousDeep Learning kya hai — ImageNet ki kahaniNext →Dimaag aur Deep Learning
4.3Chapter 4 — Deep Learning

Dimaag aur Deep Learning

Deep Learning dimaag se inspired hai. Dimaag ko samjho to network samajhna aasan hoga.

  • Dimaag ka wazan lagbhag 3.3 lbs (1.5 kg) hai, usmein lagbhag 86 billion neurons aur trillions of synapses hain.
  • Hippocampus — memories ka ghar; Alzheimer's mein yahi fail hota hai.
  • Frontal lobe — emotions, speech, creativity, judgment.
  • Cerebral cortex — thinking aur cognition; ismein neurons zyada hon to intelligence zyada.

Lekin dimaag analogue hai — woh sirf 0/1 nahi, continuous signals use karta hai. Aur woh aaj bhi mysterious hai — scientists poori tarah nahi samajh paye.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 4
← PreviousML vs DL ka farak — ghoda pehchannaNext →Artificial Neural Networks — neuron, weight, bias
4.4Chapter 4 — Deep Learning

Artificial Neural Networks — neuron, weight, bias

Neural Network ki sabse chhoti unit hai neuron (perceptron/node). Har neuron ke paas ek value, ek weight aur ek bias hota hai.

Feed-forward network: data input layer se hidden layers se hote hue output layer tak jata hai — peeche nahi mudta.

Stock example: X1 = revenue growth ≥20% (value 2), X2 = margin ≥20% (value 4). Weights: W1 = 1.9, W2 = 9.6. Bias = 1. Output = (2 × 1.9) + (4 × 9.6) + 1 — phir activation function se guzaar kar final answer.

Activation function non-linear hoti hai — bina iske network sirf seedhi line hi seekh payega. Sabse mashhoor hai sigmoid — jo value ko 0 se 1 ke beech compress karta hai, S-shape mein.

Kai hidden layers wala network Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) kehlata hai.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 4
← PreviousDimaag aur Deep LearningNext →Backpropagation — galti se seekhna
4.5Chapter 4 — Deep Learning

Backpropagation — galti se seekhna

Backpropagation ka matlab hai — galti ko peeche bhej kar weights ko sudhaarna. Yeh deep learning ki sabse badi breakthrough hai.

1986 ke paper "Learning Representations by Back-propagating Errors" ne isse mashhoor kiya.

Example: output 0.6 aaya, sahi answer 1.0 tha — error 0.4 hai. Backpropagation is error ko peeche bhejta hai aur har weight ko thoda adjust karta hai. Baar-baar dohrayo to error kam hoti jati hai.

Lekin zyada training bhi kharab hai — ek point ke baad error phir badhne lagti hai. Ise overfitting kehte hain. Beech ka point (midpoint) sabse best hota hai.

NETtalk (mid-1980s): ek network ne English text ko pronounce karna seekha — TV show par demo bhi hua.

HNC Software: credit-card fraud detection ka system banaya, billions bachaye. 2002 mein ek badi company ne ise $810 million mein khareed liya.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 4
← PreviousArtificial Neural Networks — neuron, weight, biasNext →RNN aur LSTM — sequence samajhna
4.6Chapter 4 — Deep Learning

RNN aur LSTM — sequence samajhna

Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) current input ke saath pehle wale inputs ko bhi yaad rakhta hai. Yeh sequence (kram) wale data ke liye hai — jaise text ya speech.

Example: phone par "He" type karo to system "Hello" ya "Here's" suggest karta hai — kyunki usne pehle wale words yaad rakhe hain.

LSTM (1997) — Long Short-Term Memory: RNN ka behtar version, jo lambe gaps ko handle kar sakta hai. RNN ki problem thi vanishing gradient — lambe sequence mein pehle wali jaankari kho jati thi.

Google Transformer: parallel processing karta hai — poora sentence ek saath dekhta hai, ek-ek word nahi. Isse accuracy badhi.

Google Translate: 100+ languages, roz 100 billion+ words translate karta hai. 2006 mein ML-based, 2016 mein neural MT (machine translation). Ek study mein English→Spanish accuracy 60% se badh kar 92% ho gayi.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 4
← PreviousBackpropagation — galti se seekhnaNext →CNN — images ko samajhna
4.7Chapter 4 — Deep Learning

CNN — images ko samajhna

Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) images ke liye banaya gaya hai. Fully connected network images par kaam nahi karta — har pixel ek unit ban jata hai, aur overfitting ho jata hai.

1998 ke paper "Gradient-Based Learning Applied to Document Recognition" ne CNN ko mashhoor kiya. Inspiration thi Hubel aur Wiesel ki visual cortex research — dimaag pehle lines/angles dekhta hai, phir shapes, phir objects.

Example: ek letter ki image mein 3,072 pixels hain, har pixel ki value 0–255. 5×5 ka convolutional filter image par ghumta hai aur features nikalta hai. Phir pooling se size chhota hota hai, aur aakhir mein fully connected layer faisla karta hai.

CNN ke 3 layers: Convolutional → Pooling → Fully Connected. Yahi structure aaj har image recognition system mein hai.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 4
← PreviousRNN aur LSTM — sequence samajhnaNext →GANs — do networks ki ladai
4.8Chapter 4 — Deep Learning

GANs — do networks ki ladai

Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) 2014 mein banaya gaya — ek pub mein Montreal mein idea aaya tha. Ismein do networks ek doosre se ladte hain.

  • Generator — nayi cheez banata hai (jaise nakli photo).
  • Discriminator — pehchanta hai ki photo asli hai ya nakli.

Dono baar-baar iterate karte hain — Generator behtar nakal banata hai, Discriminator behtar pehchanta hai. Aakhir mein Generator itni achhi nakal banata hai ki Discriminator bhi dhokha kha jata hai.

500+ academic papers GANs par likhe gaye. Ek mashhoor researcher ne kaha — "coolest idea in deep learning in the last 20 years" (pichle 20 saalon ka sabse cool idea).

Uses: CERN mein subatomic particles, ek teenager ne ek mashhoor artist ki style mein rap banaya, ek French collective ne 15,000 portraits (14th–20th century) se painting banayi jo Christie’s auction mein $432,000 mein biki.

Khatra: deepfakes — nakli fingerprints ("DeepMasterPrints" se 3 phone types unlock hue) aur face-swap videos. GANs se jhoothi videos banana aasan ho gaya hai.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 4
← PreviousCNN — images ko samajhnaNext →Deep Learning ke real use cases
4.9Chapter 4 — Deep Learning

Deep Learning ke real use cases

Deep Learning sirf theory nahi — yeh zindagi badal raha hai. Chaar use cases dekho:

Alzheimer's: ek university ne brain scans aur glucose levels se 6 saal pehle tak diagnose karna seekha — 92% aur 98% accuracy tests mein.

Energy: ek badi tech company ne wind power ke liye 36-ghante ke forecasts banaye — 700 MW capacity, baseline se lagbhag 20% zyada value.

Earthquakes: ek institute ne CNNs + RNNs se early-warning system banaya — "virtual seismologist". California mein roz lagbhag 50 chhote bhukamp aate hain.

Radiology: ek company (2017 mein founded) ne MRI/PET scans ko 10 guna tez kar diya. Dec 2018 mein FDA 510(k) aur CE mark mila — pehla AI nuclear-medicine device jise dono mile.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 4
← PreviousGANs — do networks ki ladaiNext →Deep Learning hardware — TPU, GPU aur chips
4.10Chapter 4 — Deep Learning

Deep Learning hardware — TPU, GPU aur chips

Deep Learning ko bahut compute chahiye — isliye naye chips bane hain.

  • Google TPU v3 (2018): 100+ petaflops, liquid cooling, on-device version bhi hai.
  • Amazon AWS Inferentia (2018): inference ke liye — ek company (2015 mein acquire ki) ke chips par based.
  • Facebook + Intel chip, Intel Nervana NNP
  • Alibaba Pingtouge chip + quantum computing (qubits)
  • Tesla chip: 6 billion transistors, 36 trillion operations per second
  • Untether AI (startup): data transfer 1,000 guna tez, $13 million funding 2019 mein (Intel bhi investor)
  • NVIDIA aaj bhi dominant hai — GPUs ke liye
SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 4
← PreviousDeep Learning ke real use casesNext →Kab DL use karein, kab nahi?
4.11Chapter 4 — Deep Learning

Kab DL use karein, kab nahi?

Deep Learning har jagah nahi chalta. Yeh tab best hai jab: data bahut ho, data text/video/image/time-series ho, compute power ho, aur outcome measure ho sake.

Toxicology example: 10,000 chemicals, 800,000 animal tests — DL animal tests se zyada predictive nikla.

Lekin DL fail bhi hota hai:

  • World Cup 2018: model ne Brazil/Spain ko winner predict kiya — France jeeta. Chaotic features ko model samajh nahi paya.
  • Self-driving car: ek car ne left turn liya kyunki aasmaan ek khaas purple rang ka tha — woh Nevada desert mein train hui thi, wahan aasmaan aisa hi dikhta tha!

Tools: SageMaker, HyperTune, SigOpt — model tuning ke liye.

Agar DL fit na ho to ML use karo — kam data chahiye, simpler hai, aur aksar zyada effective hota hai.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 4
← PreviousDeep Learning hardware — TPU, GPU aur chipsNext →Deep Learning ki kamzoriyan — 10 concerns
4.12Chapter 4 — Deep Learning

Deep Learning ki kamzoriyan — 10 concerns

2018 ke ek paper "Deep Learning: A Critical Appraisal" ne 10 concerns ginaye. Yeh samajhna zaroori hai:

  • Black Box: millions of parameters — model ne faisla kyun liya, pata nahi chalta. Regulators ko explainability chahiye.
  • Data: abstraction se nahi seekhta. "Taco" example — 5 saal ka bachcha ek example se seekh leta hai, DL ko hazaron chahiye.
  • Hierarchical Structure: asli hierarchy nahi samajhta — language understanding peeche hai.
  • Open-Ended Inference: "John promised Mary to leave" vs "John promised to leave Mary" — dono ka matlab alag hai, DL confuse ho jata hai. Woh ek novel ke characters ki motivations nahi samajh sakta.
  • Conceptual Thinking: democracy, justice, happiness, imagination — aise concepts nahi samajhta.
  • Common Sense: "computer with a sponge?" — aise sawaalon ka jawab nahi de sakta.
  • Causation: sirf correlations dhoondhta hai, cause-effect nahi.
  • Prior Knowledge: ek problem par kaam karta hai, doosri mein transfer nahi kar sakta. Basic physics bhi nahi jaanta.
  • Static: simple, rule-bound duniya mein best hai; asli duniya chaotic hai.
  • Resources: bahut zyada GPU cost; cloud option hai.

Do aur problems: Butterfly Effect (chhota change, bada result) aur Overfitting. Author ki chinta thi — DL ek "local minimum" mein phas sakta hai. Lekin woh pessimist nahi the — unka kehna tha ki researchers ko DL se aage badhna hoga.

Chapter 4 ke Key Takeaways: DL neural networks par based hai — "deep" matlab zyada hidden layers. Backpropagation se weights sudharte hain. CNN images ke liye, RNN/LSTM sequences ke liye, GANs nayi cheezein banane ke liye. DL powerful hai lekin black box hai, bahut data aur compute maangta hai, aur common sense nahi rakhta.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 4
← PreviousKab DL use karein, kab nahi?Next →RPA kya hai — UiPath ki kahani
5.1Chapter 5 — Robotic Process Automation

RPA kya hai — UiPath ki kahani

RPA ka matlab hai — software bots jo repetitive, boring kaam karte hain. "Robotic" ka matlab physical robot nahi — software robot hai.

UiPath ki kahani: 2005 mein Bucharest mein founded. 2013 mein lagbhag band hone wali thi. Phir RPA par pivot kiya — category 2000 se thi. 2018 tak fastest-growing enterprise software ban gayi: ARR $1 million se $100 million, 1,800+ customers, $448 million VC funding, $3 billion valuation.

Grand View ke hisaab se US mein RPA spend 2025 tak $3.97 billion hoga. Ek research ke hisaab se 2019 tak 10 mein se 1 startup automation-first hoga — matlab pehle se hi automation soch kar company banayenge.

Ek car company ke CEO ne kaha tha — zyada automation bhi galat hai, "Humans are underrated" (insaan ko kam mat aanko). RPA ka matlab insaan ko hatana nahi — boring kaam se aazaad karna hai.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 5
← PreviousDeep Learning ki kamzoriyan — 10 concernsNext →Unattended RPA vs RDA — do types
5.2Chapter 5 — Robotic Process Automation

Unattended RPA vs RDA — do types

RPA ke 2 main types hain:

Unattended RPA: bot poori tarah autonomous hai — background mein chalta hai, insaan ki zaroorat nahi. Exception (gadbad) aaye to insaan sambhalta hai. Example: raat mein invoices process karna.

RDA (Robotic Desktop Automation): bot employee ki madad karta hai — saath mein kaam karta hai. Example: contact center mein rep baat kar raha hai, bot side mein data nikal kar deta hai.

Bots kaise kaam karte hain? Low-code visual drag-and-drop se — coding ki zyada zaroorat nahi. Bot employee ke steps record karke wahi kaam dohrayega. OCR se handwritten notes bhi padh sakta hai. Isse "digital employee" bhi kehte hain.

Examples: HR documents, customer-service triage, insurance claims, invoices, refunds, financial reconciliation, data transfer, standard replies.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 5
← PreviousRPA kya hai — UiPath ki kahaniNext →RPA ke fayde aur nuksaan
5.3Chapter 5 — Robotic Process Automation

RPA ke fayde aur nuksaan

RPA ke fayde:

  • Customer satisfaction: 24/7 kaam, minimal errors, NPS (Net Promoter Score) up. Millennials apps prefer karte hain.
  • Scalability: spikes aur seasonal load aasani se handle karta hai.
  • Compliance built-in: har step record hota hai.
  • Dashboards/KPIs/alerts: sab kuch measure hota hai.
  • Legacy systems ke saath kaam: purane systems ko badle bina bot chala sakte ho.
  • Cleaner data: behtar data se behtar AI banti hai.

RPA ke nuksaan:

  • Kharab process ko automate karna = kharab automation. Pehle process sudhaaro, phir automate karo.
  • Brittleness: app ya process badla to bot toot jata hai.
  • Virtualized apps (Citrix) mushkil: screen snapshots se kaam karna padta hai; computer vision se madad milti hai.
  • Specialization gaps: jaise finance ke complex kaam.
  • Testing zaroori: pehle sample transactions se test karo.
  • Ownership: business managers ki zimmedari, IT ki nahi — kyunki low-tech hai.
  • Resistance: job jaane ka darr — benefits ko clearly batana zaroori hai.
SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 5
← PreviousUnattended RPA vs RDA — do typesNext →RPA se kya expect karein — ROI aur failure rate
5.4Chapter 5 — Robotic Process Automation

RPA se kya expect karein — ROI aur failure rate

RPA se kitna fayda hoga? Numbers dekhte hain:

Computer Economics ki study (~250 companies, revenues $20M–$1B+): lagbhag aadhi companies ko 18 mahine ke andar positive return mila.

US Defense Dept ke 500+ AI projects mein RPA ko "where the most efficiencies can be found" kaha gaya — sabse zyada efficiency RPA se mili.

Lekin ek research firm ke hisaab se initial RPA project failure rate 30–50% hai! Failures zyada tar planning, strategy aur expectations ki wajah se hote hain — technology ki wajah se nahi.

Isi liye hype se bacho — RPA magic wand nahi hai. Sahi expectations rakho, warna disappointment hogi.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 5
← PreviousRPA ke fayde aur nuksaanNext →Implement kaise karein — 4 steps
5.5Chapter 5 — Robotic Process Automation

Implement kaise karein — 4 steps

RPA implement karne ke 4 steps hain:

  1. Determine right functions — kaun se functions automate karne hain
  2. Assess processes — processes ko gehrai se samjho
  3. Select vendor + deploy — sahi vendor chuno aur deploy karo
  4. Set up management team — team banao jo bots ko sambhale

Agle sections mein har step detail mein hai.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 5
← PreviousRPA se kya expect karein — ROI aur failure rateNext →Sahi functions kaise chunein
5.6Chapter 5 — Robotic Process Automation

Sahi functions kaise chunein

RPA kis kaam ke liye best hai? Repetitive, structured aur routine kaam — jaise scheduling, data input/transfer, rules/workflows, cut-paste, forms bharna, search karna.

RPA kis kaam ke liye kharab hai? Jahan independent judgment chahiye, ya process baar-baar badalta ho.

Chunne ke criteria:

  • Jo areas underperform kar rahe hon
  • Jahan employee ka bahut waqt lagta ho aur error rate zyada ho
  • Jahan volume badhne par aur hiring chahiye hogi
  • Outsourcing ke candidates
  • Jahan bahut steps aur bahut apps involved hon
SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 5
← PreviousImplement kaise karein — 4 stepsNext →Processes ka assessment — pehle samjho, phir automate karo
5.7Chapter 5 — Robotic Process Automation

Processes ka assessment — pehle samjho, phir automate karo

Bahut si processes likhi hui hi nahi hoti — log bas karte hain. Bot ko har step detail mein chahiye hota hai, isliye deep assessment zaroori hai. Ismein waqt lag sakta hai; bahar ke consultants madad kar sakte hain.

Vendor tools bhi assessment mein madad karte hain. Ek company (Celonis) ne "digital MRI" banaya — jo processes ko scan karke batata hai ki kya automate ho sakta hai. Yeh UiPath, Automation Anywhere aur Blue Prism ke saath integrate hota hai.

Plan mein IT + management + departments + analytics log — sabko shamil karo.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 5
← PreviousSahi functions kaise chuneinNext →Vendor chunna aur deploy karna
5.8Chapter 5 — Robotic Process Automation

Vendor chunna aur deploy karna

Vendor apne goal ke hisaab se chuno:

  • Staff kam karna hai → unattended bots
  • Data se leverage lena hai → doosre platforms

Deployment 1 mahine se bhi kam mein ho sakta hai.

Automation fatigue: jaise-jaise aasan kaam automate hote jate hain, baaki kaam mushkil hote jate hain — returns kam hone lagte hain. Expectations ko temper karo.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 5
← PreviousProcesses ka assessment — pehle samjho, phir automate karoNext →Team setup — Center of Excellence (CoE)
5.9Chapter 5 — Robotic Process Automation

Team setup — Center of Excellence (CoE)

RPA ke liye ek Center of Excellence (CoE) banao — ek team jo bots ko manage kare.

CoE ko in sawaalon ke jawab dene honge:

  • Bot mein problem aaye to kaun intervene karega?
  • Kaun monitor karega?
  • Kaun train karega?
  • First-line support kaun dega?
  • Bots ko develop kaun karega?

Badi organizations mein roles hote hain: RPA champion/evangelist (jo RPA ko promote kare) aur RPA change manager (jo change ko manage kare).

Sprawl se bacho — har department apne bots banane lage to control kho jayega.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 5
← PreviousVendor chunna aur deploy karnaNext →RPA + AI = Cognitive RPA (CRPA)
5.10Chapter 5 — Robotic Process Automation

RPA + AI = Cognitive RPA (CRPA)

Jab RPA mein ML, Deep Learning, speech aur NLP mil jaye to use Cognitive RPA (CRPA) kehte hain. Bot sirf rules follow nahi karta — woh seekhta bhi hai.

Leaders: UiPath, Automation Anywhere, Blue Prism, NICE, Kryon.

Automation Anywhere: emails se invoice nikalna, prebuilt integrations (IBM Watson, AWS ML, Google Cloud AI).

Ek expert ne kaha: "RPA is a great way to infuse AI capabilities into business processes" — matlab RPA business mein AI daalne ka sabse aasan tareeka hai.

CRPA se kya-kya hota hai: chatbots, sahi waqt par emails/alerts, Dynamic IVR personalization, NLP se unstructured data ko structured banana.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 5
← PreviousTeam setup — Center of Excellence (CoE)Next →Real world — Microsoft royalties case (2,000% savings)
5.11Chapter 5 — Robotic Process Automation

Real world — Microsoft royalties case (2,000% savings)

Microsoft har saal billions royalties deta hai — hazaron statements, zyadatar manual. Ek RPA company ne is problem ko solve kiya.

70–80% statements straightforward/automatable the, baaki exceptions the. Setup mein lagbhag 6 hafte lage.

Result: bot ne 150 statements sirf 2.5 ghante mein kar diye — employees ko 50 ghante lagte the. 2,000% savings! Aur human error se hone wala lagbhag 5% monthly rework khatam ho gaya.

Chapter 5 ke Key Takeaways: RPA repetitive tasks ke liye hai — manual, boring kaam automate karo. CoE banao exceptions, data aur KPIs ke liye. RPA basic AI ka gateway hai — ROI ke saath.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 5
← PreviousRPA + AI = Cognitive RPA (CRPA)Next →NLP kya hai — Tay chatbot disaster
6.1Chapter 6 — Natural Language Processing

NLP kya hai — Tay chatbot disaster

Natural Language Processing (NLP) AI ka woh hissa hai jisse computer insaani bhasha samajhta hai aur use karta hai. Iski sabse badi seekh ek disaster se mili — Tay chatbot.

2014 mein ek badi tech company ne China mein Xiaoice chatbot launch kiya — WeChat par. Kuch saalon mein 40 million users ho gaye.

Success dekh kar company ne US mein bhi try kiya — Tay banaya. Improvisational comedians ko bhi bulaya taaki baat-cheet engaging ho. 23 March 2016 ko Twitter par launch hua — aur 24 ghante ke andar band karna pada. Tay racist aur sexist messages bolne laga!

Ek example mein Tay ne ek mashhoor comedian ke baare mein galat tareeke se totalitarianism aur ek dictator ka naam joda. Yeh Godwin's Law ka example tha — online discussion jitni lambi chalegi, utni zyada possibility hai ki koi dictator ka naam le de.

Company ke ek VP ne blog mein maafi maangi aur likha: "AI systems feed off of both positive and negative interactions with people... we cannot fully predict all possible human interactive misuses without learning from mistakes."

Tay ki khaasiyat thi — woh logon ki baatein repeat karta tha. Yeh approach sahi hai (pehla chatbot ELIZA bhi yahi karta tha), lekin filters zaroori hain — khaas taur par Twitter jaise free-form platform par.

Failures se hi technology seekhti hai aur evolve hoti hai.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 6
← PreviousReal world — Microsoft royalties case (2,000% savings)Next →NLP ki challenges — bhasha itni mushkil kyun?
6.2Chapter 6 — Natural Language Processing

NLP ki challenges — bhasha itni mushkil kyun?

Bhasha Turing Test ki jaan hai — aur insaan ko janwaron se alag karne wali cheez. Lekin NLP ke liye bhasha bahut complex hai:

  • Ambiguity: bhasha aksar ambiguous hoti hai. Hum nonverbal cues, tone aur environment se matlab samajhte hain. Jaise golf mein "Fore!" chillana — NLP ko context nahi pata.
  • Bhasha badalti rehti hai: Oxford English Dictionary ke hisaab se 2018 mein 1,100+ naye words/senses aaye (kul 829,000+). Naye words: "mansplain", "hangry".
  • Grammar mistakes: hum bolte waqt galtiyan karte hain, lekin log inference se samajh jate hain. NLP ke liye mushkil hai — ek shabd ke kai matlab hote hain, isse polysemy kehte hain. Example: "recognize speech" vs "wreck a nice beach" — awaaz mein ek jaise!
  • Accents aur dialects
  • Sarcasm aur emotions se matlab badal jata hai
  • Vague words: "late" ka matlab kya hai?
  • Synonyms: kai words ka matlab ek jaisa, lekin nuance alag
  • Non-linear conversations: beech mein interruptions

Phir bhi Siri, Alexa aur Cortana jaise apps ne bahut progress ki hai — khaas taur par pichle decade mein, deep learning ki wajah se.

Ek confusion: computer languages (BASIC, C, C++) bhi to bhasha hain? Haan, lekin unmein limited commands aur strict logic hoti hai. Galti karo to code crash ho jata hai. Human language bahut flexible hai — computer language bahut literal hai.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 6
← PreviousNLP kya hai — Tay chatbot disasterNext →AI bhasha kaise samajhta hai — 2 steps
6.3Chapter 6 — Natural Language Processing

AI bhasha kaise samajhta hai — 2 steps

Shuru mein NLP rules par based tha — har word/sentence ke liye rule likho. Lekin yeh complex aur scalable nahi tha. NLP shuru mein computer language jaisi hi thi!

Waqt ke saath ek general structure bana — kyunki NLP unstructured data se deal karta hai, jo unpredictable hota hai.

Step 1 — Cleaning aur Preprocessing: tokenization, stemming aur lemmatization se text ko parse karo.

Step 2 — Language Understanding aur Generation: sabse intensive part — aksar deep learning algorithms use hote hain.

Agle sections mein dono steps detail mein hain.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 6
← PreviousNLP ki challenges — bhasha itni mushkil kyun?Next →Step 1 — Tokenization (Fig 6-1)
6.4Chapter 6 — Natural Language Processing

Step 1 — Tokenization (Fig 6-1)

Tokenization ka matlab hai — text ko chhote parts (tokens) mein todna. Example: "John ate four cupcakes." — har word ek token hai.

Tokenization ke baad normalization hoti hai — text ko aasan banao: case upper/lower karna, punctuation hatana, contractions hatana.

Lekin ismein problems hain:

  • "A.I." — periods hatayein to "A I" ka matlab kya hoga?
  • Case matters: "fed" vs "Fed" (Federal Reserve). "us" vs "US" (United States).
  • White Space Problem: "New York" aur "Silicon Valley" ek token hone chahiye, do nahi.
  • Scientific words: hyphens, parentheses, Greek letters hatane se matlab kho jata hai.
  • Messy text: documents mein grammar aur spelling errors hoti hain.
  • Sentence splitting: "Mr." ya "Mrs." mein period hai — sentence wahin khatm na ho jaye.
  • Non-important words: "the", "a", "an" — inhe Stop Words filter se hataya jata hai.

Chinese aur Japanese mein to aur mushkil hai — wahan syntax hi alag hai. Tokenization pehla step hai — yahan 2 galtiyan poori process ko bigaad sakti hain.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 6
← PreviousAI bhasha kaise samajhta hai — 2 stepsNext →Stemming (Fig 6-2) — word ko root tak le jao
6.5Chapter 6 — Natural Language Processing

Stemming (Fig 6-2) — word ko root tak le jao

Stemming ka matlab hai — word ko uske root (lemma) tak le jana, affixes/suffixes hata kar. Jaise "running" → "run", "happiness" → "happi".

Search engines ke liye effective hai — word ka broader meaning mil jata hai, zyada matches milte hain, spelling errors bhi handle ho jati hain.

Lekin stemming algorithms ke mixed results hote hain. Ek badi tech company ke hisaab se:

Porter algorithm kehta hai ki 'universal' ka stem 'university' aur 'universities' jaisa hai — historically sahi ho sakta hai, lekin semantically ab relevant nahi hai. Porter stemmer yeh bhi nahi pehchanta ki 'theater' aur 'theatre' ek hi stem ke hain. Isi liye unke Watson Explorer Engine mein Porter stemmer use nahi hota.

Company ne apna proprietary stemmer banaya hai, jo customize ho sakta hai.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 6
← PreviousStep 1 — Tokenization (Fig 6-1)Next →Lemmatization (Fig 6-3) — stemming se behtar?
6.6Chapter 6 — Natural Language Processing

Lemmatization (Fig 6-3) — stemming se behtar?

Lemmatization stemming jaisi hai, lekin affixes hatane ki jagah similar root words dhoondhti hai. Example: "better" → "good". Dono ka matlab lagbhag ek hai, lekin "good" zyada clear hai.

Lemmatization ke liye system ko words ka matlab aur context samajhna padta hai. Isi liye iski performance stemming se behtar hoti hai — lekin algorithms zyada complex hote hain aur zyada computing power chahiye hoti hai.

Search aur translation mein lemmatization behtar results deti hai.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 6
← PreviousStemming (Fig 6-2) — word ko root tak le jaoNext →Step 2 — Understanding aur Generation
6.7Chapter 6 — Natural Language Processing

Step 2 — Understanding aur Generation

Text process hone ke baad, NLP system ko overall matlab samajhna hota hai. Yeh sabse mushkil part hai. Techniques:

  • Tagging Parts of Speech (POS): har word ko uska grammatical form do — noun, verb, adverb. Jaise school ki English class, automated! Noun ke types: NN (singular noun), NNP (singular proper noun), NNS (plural noun).
  • Chunking: words ko phrases mein analyse karo. Jaise noun phrase (NP) — noun jo verb ka subject ya object ho.
  • Named Entity Recognition (NER): locations, persons aur organizations ko pehchano.
  • Topic Modelling: text mein hidden patterns aur clusters dhoondho. Ek algorithm hai Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) — unsupervised learning par based. Random topics assign karo, phir iterate karke matches dhoondho.

In processes ke liye deep learning models use hote hain — isse distributional semantics kehte hain.

CNN se words ke clusters feature map mein badle jate hain — language translation, speech recognition, sentiment analysis aur Q&A mein kaam aata hai. Model sarcasm bhi detect kar sakta hai!

CNN ki problem: door ke words ke beech dependencies samajhna mushkil hai. Solutions: TDNN (time-delayed neural networks) aur DCNN (dynamic CNN). Lekin sabse zyada success RNN ko mili — kyunki woh data yaad rakhta hai.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 6
← PreviousLemmatization (Fig 6-3) — stemming se behtar?Next →Voice Recognition — Audrey se Siri tak
6.8Chapter 6 — Natural Language Processing

Voice Recognition — Audrey se Siri tak

Voice recognition ki kahani 1952 se shuru hoti hai — Bell Labs ne Audrey (Automatic Digit Recognition) banayi. Yeh phonemes pehchanti thi — bhasha ki sabse chhoti sound units. English mein 44 phonemes hain.

Audrey 0 se 9 tak ke digits pehchan sakti thi. Apne creator ki awaaz par 90% accurate, doosron par 70–80%.

Hum bolte waqt complex aur jumbled sentences bolte hain, aur tez bolte hain — average 150 words per minute. Isi liye progress slow thi. 1962 mein IBM ka Shoebox sirf 16 words, 10 digits aur 6 maths commands samajhta tha.

1980s mein breakthrough aaya — Hidden Markov Model (HMM), sophisticated statistics par based. "Dog" bolo to d, o, g sounds ko score milta hai. Waqt ke saath system behtar hota jata hai.

Lekin HMM continuous speech handle nahi kar pata tha — template matching use hoti thi: sound waves ko numbers mein badlo, frequency measure karo, close match chahiye. Voice clear aur slow honi chahiye, background noise kam.

1990s mein Dragon Dictate aaya — continuous speech mein hazaron words samajhta tha. Medicine mein transcription ke liye bahut use hua. Lekin mainstream adoption nahi hui — logon ko typing aasan lagti thi.

ML aur DL ke aane se sab badal gaya — LSTM, RNN aur deep feed-forward networks. Google ne inhe Google Voice mein lagaya (hundreds of millions smartphone users), phir Siri, Alexa aur Cortana aaye.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 6
← PreviousStep 2 — Understanding aur GenerationNext →Use case: Sales badhana — Chorus (+10% win rate)
6.9Chapter 6 — Natural Language Processing

Use case: Sales badhana — Chorus (+10% win rate)

Ek entrepreneur ne socha — roz business mein hone wali countless conversations mostly ignore ho jati hain. Kya AI isse opportunity bana sakti hai?

2015 mein unhone Chorus company banayi — sales calls se insights nikalne ke liye. Ise Conversation Cloud kaha — calls record, organize aur transcribe karo, CRM mein daalo. Waqt ke saath algorithms best practices seekhne lagte hain.

Mushkilein: billions tareeke hain sawaal poochne ke, objections uthane ke — sabko identify karna padta hai. Signals aur patterns evolve hote hain — naye competitors, products, terminology — models jaldi obsolete ho jate hain.

Ek aur mushkil: speaker separation — kaun bol raha hai, yeh pehchanna speech recognition se bhi mushkil hai (call par aksar 3 se zyada log hote hain). Chorus ne deep learning se har speaker ka "voice fingerprint" banaya — clustering par based.
