Housecall Pro ka case: ek startup jo field service management ke liye mobile tech bechta hai. Pehle har lead ke liye personalized pitch banate the — unscalable aur mixed results. Chorus se har word measure hone laga, sales rep on-script hai ya nahi — yeh bhi measure hua. Result: sales organization ki win rate 10% badh gayi.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 6
← PreviousVoice Recognition — Audrey se Siri takNext →Use case: Depression pehchanna — Stanford study
6.10Chapter 6 — Natural Language Processing

Use case: Depression pehchanna — Stanford study

Duniya bhar mein lagbhag 300 million log depression se peedit hain (WHO data). Lagbhag 15% adults apni zindagi mein kabhi na kabhi depression experience karte hain.

Healthcare services ki kami se diagnosis nahi ho pata — aur situation bigad sakti hai.

Stanford ki ek study mein ML model ne 3D facial expressions aur spoken language ko process kiya. Result: depression diagnose karne mein average error rate 3.67 (Patient Health Questionnaire / PHQ scale par). Zyada severe depression mein accuracy aur bhi zyada thi.

Researchers ne likha: "This technology could be deployed to cell phones worldwide and facilitate low-cost universal access to mental health care." — matlab yeh technology duniya bhar ke phones par chal kar sasti mental healthcare de sakti hai.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 6
← PreviousUse case: Sales badhana — Chorus (+10% win rate)Next →Use case: Content Creation — GPT-2 aur unicorns
6.11Chapter 6 — Natural Language Processing

Use case: Content Creation — GPT-2 aur unicorns

2015 mein kuch tech veterans ne OpenAI launch kiya — $1 billion funding ke saath, nonprofit ke roop mein. Goal: "to advance digital intelligence in the way that is most likely to benefit humanity as a whole, unconstrained by a need to generate financial return."

2019 mein OpenAI ne GPT-2 launch kiya — lagbhag 8 million web pages ke dataset par based. Focus: text dekh kar agla word predict karna.

Experiment: input diya — "In a shocking finding, scientist discovered a herd of unicorns living in a remote, previously unexplored valley, in the Andes Mountains. Even more surprising to the researchers was the fact that the unicorns spoke perfect English." Model ne isse 377 words ki convincing kahani bana di!

Storytelling un topics par behtar thi jo data mein zyada the — jaise Lord of the Rings aur Brexit. Technical domains par performance kharab thi.

Reading comprehension ke tests par GPT-2 ke results:

DataSetPrior RecordGPT-2 Accuracy
Winograd Schema Challenge63.7%70.70%
LAMBADA59.23%63.24%
Children's Book Test — Common Nouns85.7%93.30%
Children's Book Test — Named Entities82.3%89.05%

Table 6-1: Reading comprehension results — GPT-2 ne har test mein purana record toda. Insaan aam taur par 90%+ score karta hai.

GPT-2 ne Google ke Transformer neural network aur unsupervised learning ka use kiya tha. OpenAI ne poora model release nahi kiya — darr tha ki fake news, spoofed reviews, spam aur phishing scams badh jayenge.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 6
← PreviousUse case: Depression pehchanna — Stanford studyNext →Use case: Body Language — Affectiva aur emotions
6.12Chapter 6 — Natural Language Processing

Use case: Body Language — Affectiva aur emotions

Sirf bhasha par focus karna limiting hai — body language bhi AI model mein honi chahiye. Ek researcher ne yahi socha — computers emotions kaise detect kar sakte hain?

Unhone ek mashhoor professor ke saath mil kar ML models banaye — professor ne Affective Computing naam ki kitab likhi thi (emotions aur machines par). Neuroscience aur psychology bhi use hui. Ek aur researcher ke kaam par based — unhone facial muscles se 6 universal human emotions pehchane (wrath, grossness, scaredness, joy, loneliness, shock) — 46 movements jise Facial Action Coding System (FACS) kehte hain.

MIT Media Lab mein researcher ne ek "emotional hearing aid" banaya — wearable jo autism wale logon ko social situations mein madad karta tha. System logon ki emotions detect karke sahi reaction batata tha. New York Times ne ise 2006 ki sabse consequential innovations mein se ek mana.

Phir unhone Affectiva company launch ki — kul $54.2 million VC funding mili. Flagship product Affdex — cloud-based platform jo video ke liye audience test karta hai. Lagbhag ek-chauthai Fortune Global 500 companies use karti hain.

Doosra product: Affectiva Automotive AI — car ke andar sensing system:

  • Driver fatigue ya distraction par alert (jaise seat belt vibrate karna)
  • Driver na jaage ya gusse mein ho to semi-autonomous system ko handoff; road rage kam karne ke liye route alternatives bhi
  • Passenger ki emotions ke hisaab se music personalize karna

Models 7.5 million se zyada faces ke database par train hote hain — cultural influences aur demographic differences ko bhi account mein rakhte hain, real-time mein.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 6
← PreviousUse case: Content Creation — GPT-2 aur unicornsNext →Voice Commerce — WeChat aur $80 billion ka market
6.13Chapter 6 — Natural Language Processing

Voice Commerce — WeChat aur $80 billion ka market

Voice commerce (v-commerce) ka matlab hai — chat ya voice se kharidari karna. Iski sabse badi misaal hai WeChat.

WeChat ki company 1990s ke end mein shuru hui — pehle PC-based messenger OICQ. Phir WeChat aaya — China ka sabse bada social media platform, 1 billion+ monthly active users.

WeChat sirf messaging nahi hai — all-purpose virtual assistant hai: ride-sharing book karo, retailer par payment karo, flight reservation karo, game khelo. China mein smartphones par total usage time ka lagbhag 35% WeChat par hai. China cash-less society banne ki taraf badh raha hai — WeChat badi wajah hai.

Juniper Research ke hisaab se voice commerce market 2023 tak $80 billion tak pahunchega. Winners woh honge jinke paas bade install base hain — Amazon, Apple, Google. Lekin next-gen NLP providers ke liye bhi jagah hogi.

Marketing par asar: ek HBR article "Marketing in the Age of Alexa" mein likha tha — "AI assistants will transform how companies connect with their customers. They'll become the primary channel through which people get information, goods and services, and marketing will turn into the batter for their attention."

Yeh e-commerce revolution se bhi bada ho sakta hai — customer ke liye convenient hai: bolo aur kharido, machine tumhari aadat seekh legi. Lekin yeh winners-take-all bhi ho sakta hai — consumer sirf ek hi smart device use karega shopping ke liye. Brands ko recommendation engine mein preferred vendor banna hoga.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 6
← PreviousUse case: Body Language — Affectiva aur emotionsNext →Virtual Assistants — Siri ki kahani
6.14Chapter 6 — Natural Language Processing

Virtual Assistants — Siri ki kahani

2003 mein US Defense Department ne ek sophisticated virtual assistant banane ke liye $150 million budget diya — SRI (Stanford Research Institute) Lab ko. Lab nonprofit tha, lekin apni technologies ko startups ko license kar sakta tha (jaise inkjet printer).

Lab ke kuch members ne is technology par apni company banayi — Siri naam se. 2007 mein founded — wahi saal jab iPhone launch hua.

Real-time data, geographic search engine, credit card security — sab banana pada. Lekin sabse mushkil challenge NLP tha. Ek co-founder ne interview mein kaha:

"The hardest technical challenge with Siri was dealing with the massive amounts of ambiguity present in human language. Consider the phrase 'book 4-star restaurant in Boston' — seems very straightforward... However, when we loaded in tens of millions of business names and hundreds of thousands of cities into the system as vocabulary, the number of candidate interpretations went through the roof."

Team ne problems solve kiye aur Siri Feb 2010 mein App Store par launch hui. Ek review mein likha tha — "It's the most sophisticated voice recognition to appear on a smartphone yet."

Ek mashhoor tech CEO ne founders ko call kiya — kuch dinon mein meeting hui, aur April 2010 ke end tak acquisition ho gaya — $200 million se zyada mein. Phir 2011 mein re-release hua — CEO ke nidhan se ek din pehle.

Aaj market share: Siri 48.6%, Google Assistant 28.7%, Alexa 13.2%. US mein lagbhag 146.6 million logon ne smartphones par virtual assistants try kiye hain, aur 50 million+ ne smart speakers par. Voice technology wearables, headphones aur appliances mein bhi aa rahi hai.

Findings: voice se product search entertainment search se zyada hoti hai; productivity mein calls, emails aur alarms sabse common hain; smartphone par voice ka sabse common use driving ke waqt hota hai; sabse badi complaint — requests ko samajhne mein inconsistency.

Juniper Research ke hisaab se virtual assistants ki sankhya 2023 tak triple hokar 2.5 billion ho jayegi. Sabse tez category smart TVs hogi!

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 6
← PreviousVoice Commerce — WeChat aur $80 billion ka marketNext →Chatbots — business ke liye, aur deployment tips
6.15Chapter 6 — Natural Language Processing

Chatbots — business ke liye, aur deployment tips

Virtual assistants aur chatbots mein overlap hai — dono NLP use karte hain. Farak: chatbots zyada tar business ke liye hote hain (customer support, sales); virtual assistants har kisi ki daily activities ke liye.

Chatbots ki shuruaat 1960s mein ELIZA se hui, lekin scale par useable pichle decade mein hue.

Interesting chatbots:

  • Ushur: insurance companies ke liye — claims/bill processing aur sales enablement automate karta hai. Service center call volumes mein average 30% kami, 90% customer response rate. Apna linguistics engine LISA (Language Intelligence Services Architecture) banaya — NLP, NLU, sentiment analysis, sarcasm detection, topic detection, data extraction, translations. 60 languages support karta hai.
  • Mya: recruiting mein conversations karta hai. Time to interview aur time to hire bahut kam karta hai.
  • Jane.ai: organization ke apps/databases (Salesforce, Office, Slack, Gmail) se data nikal kar personalized answers deta hai. Employee ka lagbhag 35% waqt sirf information dhoondhne mein jata hai! Ek mortgage company ne Slack integration se brokers ki madad ki — 1,000 human labor hours per month bachaye.

Phir bhi chatbots ke mixed results hain. Ek study (500 consumers, healthcare chatbots) mein pata chala: personal information par anxiety hai, aur complex topics samajhne mein problem hai.

Chatbot deploy karne se pehle 8 baatein:

  • Set Expectations: overpromise mat karo; chatbot ko insaan mat banao. Shuruaat mein kaho — "Hi, I'm a chatbot here to help you with…"
  • Automation: chatbot poora process handle kar sakta hai, lekin log loop mein hone chahiye. Ek AI evangelist ne kaha: "The goal for chatbots is not to replace humans entirely, but to be the first line of defense" — humans complex queries handle karenge.
  • Friction: problem jaldi solve karo — kabhi-kabhi conversation ki jagah simple form behtar hota hai (jaise demo schedule karna).
  • Repetitive Processes: authentication, order status, scheduling, simple change requests — ideal hain.
  • Centralization: data integrate karo — customer ko baar-baar info repeat nahi karni chahiye.
  • Personalize: camera lens khareedne wala har shopper alag hai — assistive chatbot sahi sawaal pooch kar personalized recommendation de sakta hai.
  • Data Analytics: feedback monitor karo — satisfaction kya hai? Accuracy rate kya hai?
  • Conversational Design aur UX: website/app jaisa nahi hai — user ki personality, gender aur cultural context socho. "Voice" of company bhi. Mockups ki jagah scripts likho aur play karke dekho.

IDC ke hisaab se 2019 mein chatbots par $4.5 billion kharch hoga (kul AI spend $35.8 billion). Juniper ke hisaab se chatbot cost savings 2023 tak $7.3 billion hongi (2019 mein sirf $209 million).

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 6
← PreviousVirtual Assistants — Siri ki kahaniNext →NLP ka future — START system aur Watson
6.16Chapter 6 — Natural Language Processing

NLP ka future — START system aur Watson

1947 mein Moldova (us waqt Soviet Union) mein ek researcher paida hue. Moscow State University se computers seekhe, phir US aaye.

Unhone 80+ technical publications likhe, 2 US patents liye, aur START system banaya — sophisticated NLP capabilities ke liye. Yeh 1993 mein Web ki pehli Q&A site ka basis bana — Yahoo! aur Google se pehle.

Unki innovations IBM ke Watson ke liye bhi critical thi — 2011 mein Watson ne Jeopardy! game show ke 2 all-time champions ko hara diya.

Lekin researcher khush nahi the. Unka kehna tha — hum abhi early stages mein hain. Ek interview mein unhone kaha: "But on the other hand, these programs [like Siri and Alexa] are so incredibly stupid. So there's a feeling of being proud and being almost embarrassed. You launch something that people feel is intelligent, but it's not even close."

Woh pessimist nahi the — lekin unka kehna tha ki NLP ko "real intelligence" tak pahunchne ke liye computer science se aage dekhna hoga — neuroscience, cognitive science aur psychology ki taraf. NLP systems ko real world ke actions ko behtar samajhna hoga.

Chapter 6 ke Key Takeaways: NLP se computer insaani bhasha samajhta hai. Chatbot woh AI system hai jo logon se communicate karta hai. Challenges: ambiguity, nonverbal cues, dialects, accents, bhasha ka badalna. 2 main steps: cleaning/preprocessing aur understanding/generation. Tokenization text ko parse karta hai. Normalization text ko analysis ke liye aasan banata hai. Stemming word ko root tak le jata hai. Lemmatization similar root words dhoondhti hai. POS tagging, chunking aur topic modelling se language samajh aati hai. Phoneme bhasha ki sabse chhoti sound unit hai.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 6
← PreviousChatbots — business ke liye, aur deployment tipsNext →Robot kya hai — Flippy aur 'robot' shabd ki kahani
7.1Chapter 7 — Physical Robots

Robot kya hai — Flippy aur 'robot' shabd ki kahani

Pasadena mein ek restaurant mein log khane ki jagah ke peeche glass ke saamne bheed lagaye photo le rahe the. Wajah thi Flippy — ek AI-powered robot jo burgers pakata hai.

Flippy khane ki quality consistency se behtar karta hai aur production cost kam karta hai — aur regulatory standards ka poora khayal rakhta hai. Lab mein engineers Flippy ka "brain" bana rahe the, jo cloud par upload hota tha. Capabilities: utensils aur grill dhona, cooking problems se adapt karna, raw meat aur cooked meat ke liye alag spatula use karna, fryer mein baskets rakhna — sab real-time mein.

IDC ke hisaab se robotics aur drones par kharcha $115.7 billion (2019) se badh kar $210.3 billion (2022) hoga — 20.2% CAGR. Do-tihai kharcha hardware par hoga.

"Robot" shabd ki kahani: 1921 mein ek play "Rossum's Universal Robots" mein aaya — factory mein organic matter se robots bante the, jo aakhir mein humans ke khilaf bagawat kar dete the. "Robot" Czech shabd robata se aaya hai — matlab forced labor (zabardasti ka kaam).

Robot ki 4 pehchan:

  • Physical: size chhota bhi (body ke andar jaane wala) aur bada bhi (industrial systems, flying machines, underwater vessels). Energy source chahiye — battery, electricity ya solar.
  • Act: kuch action le sake — item uthana ya bolna.
  • Sense: environment samajh sake — sensors aur feedback systems se.
  • Intelligence: full AI nahi, lekin programmed actions le sake.

Aaj robot banana mushkil nahi hai — ek website par kits $10 se lekar $35,750 tak milte hain (sabse mehenga Dr. Robot Jaguar V6 Tracked Mobile Platform).

Ek heart-warming story: 2 saal ka ek bachcha rare genetic condition ki wajah se immobile tha. Parents ko special electric wheelchair ka reimbursement nahi mila. Ek high school ke students ne ek mahine mein uske liye robot wheelchair bana di — ab woh apne do corgis ke peeche ghar mein ghoom sakta hai!

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 7
← PreviousNLP ka future — START system aur WatsonNext →Robot ke andar kya hota hai — sensors, actuators, computer
7.2Chapter 7 — Physical Robots

Robot ke andar kya hota hai — sensors, actuators, computer

Har robot mein 3 main interactions hote hain — sense karna, act karna aur sochna.

  • Sensors: camera ya Lidar (light detection and ranging) — laser scanner se 3D images banata hai. Sound, touch, taste aur smell ke sensors bhi ho sakte hain. Insaan se aage — night vision ya chemicals detect karna. Sensor ki jaankari controller ko jati hai, jo arm ya doosre parts ko activate karta hai.
  • Actuators: electro-mechanical devices jaise motors — arms, legs, head aur movable parts ko hilate hain.
  • Computer: memory aur processors — sensor inputs ko process karte hain. Advanced robots mein AI chips ya cloud connection bhi hota hai.

Robot operate karne ke 2 tareeke:

  • Telerobot: human remote control karta hai.
  • Autonomous robot: khud navigate karta hai — AI se.
SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 7
← PreviousRobot kya hai — Flippy aur 'robot' shabd ki kahaniNext →Shakey — pehla mobile, thinking robot
7.3Chapter 7 — Physical Robots

Shakey — pehla mobile, thinking robot

Pehla mobile, thinking robot tha Shakey. Naam isliye pada kyunki woh hilta tha — project manager ne kaha tha: "We worked for a month trying to find a good name for it... and then one of us said, 'Hey, it shakes like hell and moves around, let's just call it Shakey.'"

Stanford Research Institute (SRI) ne DARPA funding se 1966–1972 tak Shakey par kaam kiya. Woh 5 feet se bada tha, wheels se chalta tha, sensors aur cameras se touch karta tha. Wirelessly DEC PDP-10 aur PDP-15 computers se juda tha — teletype se commands diye jate the.

Shakey algorithms se navigate karta tha — darwaze bhi band kar leta tha! Iske peeche kai AI breakthroughs the — jaise STRIPS (automated planning) aur A* algorithm (shortest path, kam compute mein).

1960s ke end mein space program ki wajah se Shakey ko bahut publicity mili — ek magazine ne use "first electronic person" kaha.

Lekin 1972 mein AI Winter ke saath DARPA ne funding kheench li. Phir bhi Shakey tech history ka hissa hai — 2004 mein Robot Hall of Fame mein induct hua.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 7
← PreviousRobot ke andar kya hota hai — sensors, actuators, computerNext →Industrial robots — Unimate, GM aur Moravec paradox
7.4Chapter 7 — Physical Robots

Industrial robots — Unimate, GM aur Moravec paradox

Robots ka pehla real-world use manufacturing mein hua — lekin adoption mein waqt laga.

Kahani shuru hoti hai ek inventor se — high school bhi poora nahi kiya, lekin engineering mein genius the. Microwave ovens, barcodes aur automatic doors ke core systems banaye — zindagi mein 40+ patents.

1950s ke shuru mein unhe Unimate naam ke programmable robot ka patent mila. Har investor ne mana kar diya. 1957 mein ek cocktail party mein unki mulaqat ek engineer-businessman se hui — jaise do tech founders ki mulaqat. Engineer ko science fiction pasand thi, aur woh chahte the ki Unimate society ko fayda pahunchaye.

Funding milne mein ek saal laga. Phir Unimate ko General Motors (GM) ko 1961 mein becha gaya. Robot bulky tha (2,700 pounds, 7-foot arm), lekin welding, spraying aur gripping — accurately, 24/7 karta tha. Logon ko khatarnak kaam nahi karna padta tha.

1966 mein engineer The Tonight Show par aaye — Unimate ne golf ball perfectly putt kiya aur beer bhi pour ki. Host ne mazak mein kaha ki machine "kisi ki job le sakti hai".

GM ka $90 billion disaster (1980s): CEO ne "lights out" factory ka sapna dekha — robots andhere mein cars banayenge! $90 billion kharch kiye, ek joint venture banaya jo duniya ka sabse bada robot manufacturer bana. Lekin disaster hua — robots ne darwaze weld karke band kar diye, cars ki jagah khud ko paint kar diya! Unions bhi naraaz hui.

Tesla ka case: ek mashhoor CEO ne April 2018 mein kaha — Model 3 banate waqt bahut zyada robots use kiye, process slow ho gaya. Zyada log hone chahiye the. Tesla ka existence hi khatre mein pad gaya tha.

Isi ko Moravec paradox kehte hain: "It is comparatively easy to make computers exhibit adult level performance on intelligence tests or playing checkers, and difficult or impossible to give them the skills of a one-year-old when it comes to perception and mobility." Matlab jo insaan ke liye aasan hai (chalna, dekhna), woh robot ke liye mushkil hai — aur jo insaan ke liye mushkil hai (chess, maths), woh computer ke liye aasan hai.

Phir bhi industry badi hai — 2018 mein North America mein 35,880 industrial aur commercial robots ship hue. Auto industry ka hissa lagbhag 53% tha, lekin kam ho raha hai. Chhoti-medium companies bhi robots use kar rahi hain.

Costs bhi gir rahi hain — ek research ke hisaab se 2025 tak 65% reduction, average $11,000 se kam per device. Yeh Wright's Law par based hai — har baar jab production double hota hai, cost ek consistent percentage se girti hai.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 7
← PreviousShakey — pehla mobile, thinking robotNext →AI + robots — Osaro, Dactyl, MIT, Google
7.5Chapter 7 — Physical Robots

AI + robots — Osaro, Dactyl, MIT, Google

Deep learning ke bawajood robots mein AI slow progress kar rahi hai. Kaaran: research zyada tar software models (jaise image recognition) par focus karti hai. Physical robots ko real-time mein noisy environment samajhna hota hai — SLAM (simultaneous localization and mapping) chahiye, unknown environment mein apni location track karte hue. Iske liye naye neural network algorithms aur quantum computers bhi chahiye ho sakte hain.

Phir bhi progress hai — khaas taur par reinforcement learning se:

  • Osaro: robots ko jaldi seekhne deta hai — "learned sensor fusion" aur high-level planning. Ek robot ne sirf 5 seconds mein seekha ki chicken ko kaise uthana aur rakhna hai (poultry factories ke liye). Drones, autonomous vehicles aur IoT mein bhi use ho sakta hai.
  • OpenAI Dactyl: human-like dexterity wala robot hand. Real-world interactions nahi — simulations se train hua. Ise "domain randomization" kehte hain — robot ko kai scenarios dikhaye, woh bhi jo bahut kam probability wale hon. Simulations mein lagbhag 100 saal ki problem solving hui! System ne aise human hand actions seekhe jo preprogrammed nahi the — jaise finger slide karna. Delayed sensor readings aur multiple objects bhi handle karta hai.
  • MIT: robot ko environment samajhne ke liye hazaron samples chahiye hote hain — jaise mug detect karna. MIT ke professors ne neural network se sirf kuch key features par focus kiya — samples kam lage. Research early stage mein hai, lekin impactful ho sakti hai.
  • Google: 2013 se robotics companies khareedne laga, lekin results disappointing rahe. Ab focus simpler AI-driven robots par hai — naya division Robotics at Google. Ek robot bin mein se requested item ko three-fingered hand se uthata hai — 85% accuracy. Insaan 80% karta hai!
SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 7
← PreviousIndustrial robots — Unimate, GM aur Moravec paradoxNext →Cobots — insaan aur robot saath mein
7.6Chapter 7 — Physical Robots

Cobots — insaan aur robot saath mein

Poori automation shayad jaldi nahi hogi. Bada trend hai cobots — robots jo logon ke saath kaam karte hain. Machine aur insaan dono ke fayde milte hain.

Sabse bada leader hai Amazon. 2012 mein company ne Kiva (industrial robot manufacturer) ko $775 million mein khareeda. Tab se 25+ fulfillment centers mein lagbhag 100,000 systems deploy kiye — inventory capacity mein 40% improvement.

Amazon Robotics: "automates fulfilment center operations using various methods of robotic technology including autonomous mobile robots, sophisticated control software, language perception, power management, computer vision, depth sensing, machine learning, object recognition, and semantic understanding of commands."

Warehouse mein robots floor par tezi se ghoom kar storage pods locate aur lift karte hain. Log bhi zaroori hain — individual products ko pehchanne aur pick karne mein insaan behtar hai.

Setup complicated hai — warehouse employees Robotic Tech Vests pehente hain taaki robots unhe kuchal na dein! Vest se robot insaan ko pehchan leta hai.

Cobots ki problems: employees ko darr rehta hai ki machines unhe replace kar dengi. Log khud ko "cog in the wheel" (machine ka chhota hissa) mehsoos karte hain — morale gir sakta hai. Kya log robots se bond kar sakte hain? Shayad nahi — khaas taur par industrial robots se, jinmein human qualities nahi hain.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 7
← PreviousAI + robots — Osaro, Dactyl, MIT, GoogleNext →Use case: Security — Cobalt Robotics aur RaaS
7.7Chapter 7 — Physical Robots

Use case: Security — Cobalt Robotics aur RaaS

Do robotics experts (Google aur SpaceX mein kaam kar chuke) ne 2016 mein apna venture shuru karne se pehle kai companies se baat ki. Ek common theme mili: facilities ki physical security — shaam 5 baje ke baad bina mehenga security guards rakhe kaise suraksha karein?

Result: Cobalt Robotics launch hua. Timing perfect thi — computer vision, machine learning aur robotics mein progress ho rahi thi.

Traditional security (cameras, sensors) static hoti hai — real-time response achha nahi hota. Robot mobile hai aur intelligent hai — proactive ho sakta hai.

Lekin log bhi loop mein hain — robot 24/7 data processing aur sensing karta hai, log critical thinking aur alternatives weigh karte hain.

Business model bhi innovative hai — Robotics as a Service (RaaS). Subscription par charge karte hain, isliye devices customers ke liye zyada affordable hain.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 7
← PreviousCobots — insaan aur robot saath meinNext →Use case: Floor-scrubbing robots — Brain Corp aur Walmart
7.8Chapter 7 — Physical Robots

Use case: Floor-scrubbing robots — Brain Corp aur Walmart

Sabse interesting robot applications mundane (roz-marra ke) categories mein hain — repetitive kaam mein machines best hain.

Brain Corp (2009 mein founded) ne pehle Qualcomm aur DARPA ke liye technology banayi. Phir ML aur computer vision se self-driving robots banaye. Kul $125 million funding mili (Qualcomm, SoftBank jaise investors se).

Flagship robot Auto-C floors scrub karta hai. AI system BrainOS (cloud-connected) se complex environments mein autonomously navigate karta hai — button dabao, aur Auto-C route map kar leta hai.

2018 ke end mein Brain ne Walmart ke saath agreement kiya — hundreds of stores mein 1,500 Auto-C robots deploy karne ka. Airports aur malls mein bhi robots deploy hue.

Walmart shelf-scanning robots bhi laga raha hai — inventory management ke liye. US mein lagbhag 4,600 stores hain — robots ka bada impact hoga.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 7
← PreviousUse case: Security — Cobalt Robotics aur RaaSNext →Use case: Online Pharmacy — PillPack ($1B Amazon deal)
7.9Chapter 7 — Physical Robots

Use case: Online Pharmacy — PillPack ($1B Amazon deal)

Ek second-generation pharmacist ko logon ki prescription manage karne ki frustration ka pehle se pata tha. Solution: digital pharmacy banao?

Unhone ek MIT engineer ko tech co-founder banaya. 2013 mein PillPack bani. App ya website se sign up karo — insurance info daalo, prescription needs batao, deliveries schedule karo. Package mein dose instructions aur har pill ki image hoti thi. Pills labels ke saath presorted containers mein aati thi.

Iske peeche tha PharmacyOS — 80,000-square-foot warehouse mein robots ka network, jo prescriptions ko efficiently sort aur package karta tha. Licensed pharmacists bhi the — compliance ke liye.

June 2018 mein Amazon ne PillPack ko lagbhag $1 billion mein khareed liya. News par CVS aur Walgreens ke shares gir gaye — darr tha ki e-commerce giant healthcare mein bada khel khelne wala hai.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 7
← PreviousUse case: Floor-scrubbing robots — Brain Corp aur WalmartNext →Use case: Robot Scientists — Adam aur Eve
7.10Chapter 7 — Physical Robots

Use case: Robot Scientists — Adam aur Eve

Nayi dawa banana bahut mehenga hai — Tufts Center ke hisaab se average $2.6 billion per approved compound. Aur market tak pahunchne mein ek decade se zyada lag sakta hai — regulations ki wajah se.

Do universities ke researchers ne 2009 mein Adam launch kiya — robot scientist jo drug discovery mein madad karta hai. Kuch saal baad Eve aayi — next-generation robot.

System hypotheses banata hai, test karta hai, experiments chalata hai. Sirf brute-force nahi — 10,000+ compounds per day screen kar sakta hai. Deep learning se woh compounds pehchanta hai jinmein sabse zyada potential hai.

Example: Eve ne dikhaya ki triclosan (toothpaste mein plaque rokne wala element) malaria ke parasite growth ke khilaf effective ho sakta hai — yeh important hai kyunki malaria existing therapies se resistant hota ja raha hai.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 7
← PreviousUse case: Online Pharmacy — PillPack ($1B Amazon deal)Next →Humanoid aur consumer robots — Sophia, Atlas, Pepper, Jibo
7.11Chapter 7 — Physical Robots

Humanoid aur consumer robots — Sophia, Atlas, Pepper, Jibo

1960s ke cartoon The Jetsons mein Rosie thi — robot maid jo hamesha vacuum cleaner pakde rehti thi. Kaun nahi chahega aisi robot? Lekin Rosie jaisi robot ghar mein aane mein abhi waqt hai. Consumer robots abhi early days mein hain — sirf kuch human features hain.

Notable examples:

  • Sophia: Hong Kong ki company Hanson Robotics ne banayi — sabse famous. Late 2017 mein Saudi Arabia ne use citizenship di! Sophia ek mashhoor actress jaisi dikhti hai, chal aur bol sakti hai. Eye contact sustain karna jaise subtleties bhi hain.
  • Atlas: Boston Dynamics ne 2013 ki garmi mein launch kiya. Backflips kar sakta hai, gir kar khud uth sakta hai.
  • Pepper: SoftBank Robotics ka humanoid — customer service ke liye, retail locations par. Gestures use karta hai, multiple languages bol sakta hai.

Jab humanoid technologies realistic hongi, society badlegi — pyaar aur dosti ke norms evolve honge. Smartphones ne hi dikha diya ki technology relationships kaise badal deti hai. Ek survey mein lagbhag 10% Millennials ne kaha ki woh smartphone chhodne ki jagah apni pinky finger sacrifice kar denge!

Social robots: life-like robot jo dost ya saathi jaisa ban sake. Ek example hai ElliQ — tablet + chhota robot head. Akele rehne wale, khaas taur par elderly ke liye. Baat kar sakta hai, medicine lene ki reminder de sakta hai, family se video chat karwa sakta hai.

Jibo ka downfall: pehla social robot for home. Company ne $72.7 million VC funding raise ki. Lekin product delays aur knock-offs ki wajah se 2018 mein bankruptcy file ki, aur April 2019 tak servers band ho gaye. Reddit par kai disheartened owners ne posts likhe.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 7
← PreviousUse case: Robot Scientists — Adam aur EveNext →Three Laws of Robotics — Asimov ke niyam
7.12Chapter 7 — Physical Robots

Three Laws of Robotics — Asimov ke niyam

Ek prolific science-fiction writer ne 1942 ki short story "Runaround" mein Three Laws of Robotics diye:

  1. First Law: Robot kisi insaan ko nuksaan nahi pahunchayega, ya inaction se insaan ko nuksaan nahi hone dega.
  2. Second Law: Robot insaanon ke orders manega — jab tak woh First Law se conflict na karein.
  3. Third Law: Robot apni existence ko protect karega — jab tak woh First ya Second Law se conflict na kare.

Baad mein writer ne ek aur law joda — Zeroth Law: "A robot may not harm humanity, or, by inaction, allow humanity to come to harm." Yeh sabse important mana gaya.

Unhone aur short stories likhi jo dikhati thi ki yeh laws complex situations mein kaise kaam karte hain — yeh I, Robot kitab mein collect hui. Sab stories 21st century mein set thi.

Three Laws writer ki reaction thi — science fiction mein robots ko malevolent (bure) dikhaya jata tha. Unhe yeh unrealistic laga. Unhe foresight thi ki robots ki power ko control karne ke liye ethical rules banenge.

Aaj Asimov ka vision sach hone laga hai — ethical principles explore karna achha idea hai. Yeh zaroori nahi ki unka approach hi sahi ho — lekin yeh achhi shuruaat hai, khaas taur par jab robots AI ki wajah se smart aur personal ho rahe hain.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 7
← PreviousHumanoid aur consumer robots — Sophia, Atlas, Pepper, JiboNext →Cybersecurity aur robots — naya khatra
7.13Chapter 7 — Physical Robots

Cybersecurity aur robots — naya khatra

Cybersecurity robots ke liye abhi badi problem nahi hai — lekin jald hi hogi. Kaaran: robots cloud se connect ho rahe hain. IoT aur autonomous cars ke saath bhi yahi hai. Wireless updates ki wajah se malware, viruses aur ransomware ka khatra hai. Electric vehicles charging network se bhi attack ho sakte hain.

Tumhara data vehicle ke andar reh sakta hai! Agar car wreck ho jaye ya tum use bech do, to video, navigation details aur paired smartphone ke contacts doosron ko mil sakte hain. Ek white hat hacker ne junkyards se kai Tesla models ka data nikal liya tha. Company data wipe karne ka option deti hai, aur data collection se opt out bhi kar sakte ho — lekin phir over-the-air (OTA) updates jaise fayde nahi milenge.

Agar robot hack ho jaye to implications devastating ho sakti hain — imagine karo hacker ne manufacturing line, supply chain ya robotic surgery system ko infiltrate kar liya. Jaan khatre mein pad sakti hai.

Phir bhi robots ki cybersecurity mein investment kam hai — sirf kuch companies (jaise Karamba Security, Cybereason) is par focus karti hain. Jaise-jaise problems badhengi, VCs aur legacy cybersecurity firms invest karenge.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 7
← PreviousThree Laws of Robotics — Asimov ke niyamNext →Robots ko program karna — ROS aur simulators
7.14Chapter 7 — Physical Robots

Robots ko program karna — ROS aur simulators

Intelligent robots banana aasan hota ja raha hai — systems saste ho rahe hain aur naye software platforms aa rahe hain. Sabse bada hai Robot Operating System (ROS) — industry ka standard ban raha hai. Origins 2007 mein — Stanford Artificial Intelligence Laboratory mein open source project.

Naam ke bawajood ROS asli operating system nahi hai — yeh middleware hai jo robot ke critical parts manage karta hai: planning, simulations, mapping, localization, perception, prototypes. Modular hai — jo functions chahiye wahi chuno. Development time bahut kam ho jata hai.

ROS ki global community hai — 3,000+ packages hain.

Microsoft ne late 2018 mein Windows ke liye ROS version announce kiya. Ek principal software engineer ne blog mein likha: "As robots have advanced, so have the development tools. We see robotics with artificial intelligence as universally accessible technology to augment human abilities." ROS Visual Studio ke saath use ho sakta hai, aur Azure cloud (AI Tools ke saath) se connect hota hai.

Intelligent robots banane ka process software AI se alag hai — physical device bhi chahiye, aur test karne ka tareeka bhi. Aksar simulation se test karte hain. Kuch developers cardboard models se shuru karte hain — physical requirements samajhne ke liye.

Virtual simulators: MuJoCo, Gazebo, MORSE, V-REP — sophisticated 3D graphics se movements aur real-world physics handle karte hain.

AI models kaise banayein robots ke liye? Software algorithms jaisa hi approach hai (Chapter 2 wala). Lekin robot ka fayda hai — woh apne sensors se continuously data collect karta hai, jo AI ko evolve karne mein madad karta hai.

Cloud bhi critical hai — Amazon ne AWS par AWS RoboMaker launch kiya: robots ko bina zyada configuration ke build, test aur deploy karo. ROS par based hai, ML/analytics/monitoring services use kar sakte ho. Prebuilt virtual 3D worlds hain — retail stores, indoor rooms, race tracks! Phir OTA system se secure deployment aur periodic updates.

Google bhi apna robot cloud platform launch karne wala tha (2019 mein expected).

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 7
← PreviousCybersecurity aur robots — naya khatraNext →Robots ka future — iRobot aur Rethink ki kahani
7.15Chapter 7 — Physical Robots

Robots ka future — iRobot aur Rethink ki kahani

Robotics industry ke ek giant ne 1990 mein iRobot co-found kiya. Aasan nahi tha — 2002 tak Roomba vacuuming robot launch hua, jo hit hua. Aaj iRobot ki market value $3.2 billion hai aur 2018 revenues $1 billion se zyada.

Unhi founder ne Rethink Robotics bhi launch ki — vision ambitious tha. 2010 mein $20 million funding ke waqt unhone kaha: "Our robots will be intuitive to use, intelligent and highly flexible. They'll be easy to buy, train, and deploy and will be unbelievably inexpensive. [Rethink Robotics] will change the definition of how and where robots can be used, dramatically expanding the robot marketplace."

Lekin challenges aaye — cobots ka idea pioneering tha, lekin safety par focus ki wajah se precision aur accuracy industrial customers ke standards par nahi thi. Demand tepid (thandi) rahi. Oct 2018 tak company ke paas cash khatm ho gaya aur doors band karne pade. Kul lagbhag $150 million raise kiye the (Goldman Sachs, Sigma Partners, GE, Bezos Expeditions jaise investors se). Intellectual property ek German automation firm (HAHN Group) ko bech di gayi.

Yeh dikhata hai ki smartest tech log bhi galat ho sakte hain. Robotics market mein unique complexities hain — progress choppy aur volatile ho sakti hai.

Ek Cobalt Robotics ke CTO ne kaha: "While the industry has made progress in the last decade, robotics hasn't yet realized its full potential. Any new technology will create a wave of numerous new companies, but only a few will survive and turn into lasting businesses. The Dot-Com bust killed the majority of internet companies, but Google, Amazon, and Netflix all survived. What robotics companies need to do is to be upfront about what their robots can do for customers today, overcome Hollywood stereotypes of robots as the bad guys, and demonstrate a clear ROI (Return On Investment) to customers."

Chapter 7 ke Key Takeaways: Robot action le sakta hai, environment sense kar sakta hai, aur kuch intelligence rakhta hai. Sensors, actuators (motors) aur computers key functions hain. 2 tareeke: telerobot (human control) aur autonomous robot (AI). Robots banana bahut complex hai — Moravec paradox ki wajah se. AI ka impact slow hai, lekin reinforcement learning se progress tez ho rahi hai. Cobots insaan ke saath kaam karte hain. Costs gir rahi hain, aur subscription models (RaaS) adoption badha rahe hain. Consumer robots abhi early stage mein hain. Three Laws robots ko safe rakhne ka framework hai. Cybersecurity aane wala bada khatra hai. ROS industry standard hai.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 7
← PreviousRobots ko program karna — ROS aur simulatorsNext →AI implement karna — Facebook case se sabak
8.1Chapter 8 — Implementation of AI

AI implement karna — Facebook case se sabak

March 2019 mein ek attacker ne Facebook par live-stream karke 50 logon ko do mosques mein maar diya. Video lagbhag 4,000 baar dekha gaya aur attack ke 29 minute baad tak band nahi hua. Phir doosre platforms par upload hokar millions baar dekha gaya.

Yeh AI ki failure ka stark example tha. Facebook ke ek VP ne blog mein likha: AI systems 'training data' par based hote hain — kisi content ko detect karne ke liye hazaron examples chahiye hote hain. Nudity, terrorist propaganda aur graphic violence ke liye bahut examples the, isliye detection achha tha. Lekin is khaas video ke liye system trigger nahi hua — is type ke content ka bahut data chahiye hota hai, aur aise events (shukr hai) rare hote hain. Doosri challenge: aise content ko visually similar innocuous content se alag karna — jaise live-streamed video games ke hazaron videos flag ho jayein to reviewers important real-world videos miss kar sakte hain.

Bad actors ne edited versions re-upload karke AI ko foil bhi kiya.

Yeh sabak hai: sabse sophisticated companies ko bhi AI implement karne mein major challenges hote hain. Solid planning chahiye, aur yeh samajhna chahiye ki problems aayengi hi. Senior managers par results ka pressure hota hai — lekin jaldi mat karo.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 8
← PreviousRobots ka future — iRobot aur Rethink ki kahaniNext →Do approaches — vendor software vs in-house models
8.2Chapter 8 — Implementation of AI

Do approaches — vendor software vs in-house models

Company mein AI use karne ke 2 tareeke hain: vendor software use karo, ya in-house models banao. Pehla sabse common hai — aur kai companies ke liye kaafi hai.

Tum shayad pehle se hi AI use kar rahe ho — Salesforce, Microsoft, Google, Workday, Adobe ya SAP ke software mein AI capabilities pehle se hain. Pehle unka poora fayda uthao.

Salesforce Einstein (Sept 2016): CRM platform mein seamlessly embedded — sales, service, marketing aur commerce ke liye predictive aur personalized actions. Company ise "personal data scientist" kehti hai — drag and drop se workflows banao. Capabilities:

  • Predictive Scoring: lead convert hone ki likelihood dikhata hai.
  • Sentiment Analysis: social media analyse karke brand ke baare mein log kya sochte hain, yeh batata hai.
  • Smart Recommendations: leads ke liye sabse ideal products dikhata hai.

Lekin prebuilt features ke bawajood issues hain. Ek software company ke evangelist ne kaha: "We have been building AI functions into our applications during the past few years and this has been a great learning experience. But to make the technology work, the users must use the software right. If the sales people are not inputting information correctly, then the results will likely be off. We also found that there should be at least three months of usage for the models to get trained. And besides, even if your employees are doing everything right, this does not mean that the AI predictions will be perfect. Always take things with a grain of salt."

In-house models banana bada commitment hai — yahi is chapter ka focus hai.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 8
← PreviousAI implement karna — Facebook case se sabakNext →Education aur training — pehle seekho, phir banao
8.3Chapter 8 — Implementation of AI

Education aur training — pehle seekho, phir banao

Chahe approach koi bhi ho, AI implementation ki shuruaat education aur training se honi chahiye. Technical ho ya non-technical — sabko AI ki core understanding honi chahiye. Online resources bahut hain — Lynda, Udacity, Udemy par hundreds of high-quality AI courses hain.

Adobe ka example: company ke paas incredibly talented engineers hain, lekin kai ko AI ka background nahi tha. Company ne 6-month certification program banaya — 2018 mein 5,000 engineers train kiye. Goal: har engineer ke andar data scientist ko jagana.

Program mein online courses + in-person sessions — technical topics ke saath strategy aur ethics bhi. Senior computer scientists se help bhi milti thi.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 8
← PreviousDo approaches — vendor software vs in-house modelsNext →Bias ka khatra — Amazon recruiting tool aur ethics boards
8.4Chapter 8 — Implementation of AI

Bias ka khatra — Amazon recruiting tool aur ethics boards

AI implementation ka sabse bada risk hai bias — yeh model mein aasani se ghus jata hai.

Amazon ka case: company ne 2017 mein apna AI-powered recruiting software band kar diya — woh males ko hire karne mein biased tha. Kaaran training data tha — zyadatar resume submissions males se aaye the, isliye data skewed tha. Company ne model tweak karne ki koshish ki, lekin results gender neutral nahi hue.

Yeh sirf galat faislon ki baat nahi thi — company discrimination claims jaise legal liability ke liye bhi expose ho rahi thi.

Isi liye kai companies ethics boards bana rahi hain. Lekin yeh bhi mushkil hai — jo ek ke liye ethical hai, woh doosre ke liye nahi ho sakta. Example: Google ne apna ethics board launch ke lagbhag ek hafte mein band kar diya — ek member ko lekar backlash hua (woh ek conservative think tank se the).

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 8
← PreviousEducation aur training — pehle seekho, phir banaoNext →Step 1 — Problem pehchano (pehla AI project chunne ke 4 rules)
8.5Chapter 8 — Implementation of AI

Step 1 — Problem pehchano (pehla AI project chunne ke 4 rules)

AI project shuru karne se pehle data saaf aur structured hona chahiye (Chapter 2 dekho). Phir 5 steps hain: (1) Problem pehchano, (2) Team banao, (3) Tools chuno, (4) Model banao (Chapter 3), (5) Deploy aur monitor karo.

Ek badi IT consulting company (132,000 employees, 44 countries, aadhe Fortune 500 customers) ke CTO ne kaha: "Business leaders need to understand and realize that the adoption of Artificial Intelligence is a journey and not a sprint. It is critical that the people driving AI adoption within an enterprise remain realistic about the timeframe and what AI is capable of doing. The relationship between humans and AI is mutually empowering, and any AI implementation may take some time before it starts to make a positive and significant impact."

Shuru mein experimental approach lo — pilot program, "crawl and walk phase". Technology par zyada focus mat karo — pehle clear business case chahiye. Socho:

  • Decisions aksar ad hoc aur guess par hoti hain — AI se data-driven decisions kahan sabse zyada fayda denge?
  • RPA ki tarah repetitive aur mundane tasks AI ke liye best hain.
  • Chatbots aasan shuruaat hain — customer service jaise specific use cases ke liye.

Ek mashhoor AI researcher (Landing AI ke CEO, ex-Google Brain head) ke 4 rules — pehla AI project chunne ke liye:

  • Quick Win: project 6–12 mahine mein poora ho, success ki high probability ho. 2 projects rakho — win ke odds badhte hain.
  • Meaningful: transformative hona zaroori nahi — lekin results notable hone chahiye. Value aati hai lower costs, higher revenues, naye business extensions ya risk mitigation se.
  • Industry-Specific Focus: subscription business hai to churn kam karne wala AI system achhi shuruaat hai.
  • Data: data ki quantity se options limit mat karo — successful AI project mein sirf 100 data points bhi kaafi ho sakte hain. Lekin data high quality aur fairly clean hona chahiye.

Human-machine "tango": AI huge amounts of data ko kam errors ke saath tez process karta hai, predictions aur anomaly detection mein best hai. Lekin insaan creativity, abstraction aur concepts samajhne mein behtar hai. Example: ek security robotics company ke robots thermal-imaging se dark office mein insaan ko detect karte hain — lekin respond kaise karna hai, yeh human operator decide karta hai. AI se galti ki gravity socho — malicious intruder miss karna false alarm se bahut bura hai.

KPIs clear rakho aur diligently measure karo — jaise chatbot ke liye resolution rate aur customer satisfaction. IT assessment bhi karo — legacy systems zyada hon to AI implement karna mushkil aur mehenga hoga.

Symrise ka case: 200+ saal purani German company, flavors aur fragrances ki global producer (30,000+ products). IBM ki madad se AI se naye perfumes banane lage. IT infrastructure retool karna pada, models fine-tune karne mein waqt laga — lekin extensive dataset se precision mili. Company ke president ne kaha: "Now our perfumers can work with an AI apprentice by their side, that can analyze thousands of formulas and historical data to identify patterns and predict novel combinations, helping to make them more productive, and accelerate the design process by guiding them toward formulas that have never been seen before."

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 8
← PreviousBias ka khatra — Amazon recruiting tool aur ethics boardsNext →Step 2 — Team banao (two-pizza rule)
8.6Chapter 8 — Implementation of AI

Step 2 — Team banao (two-pizza rule)

Initial AI team kitni badi ho? Ek mashhoor rule hai — "two pizza rule": team itni chhoti ho ki 2 pizzas se sabko khana mil jaye.

Team banane mein jaldi mat karo. Sabko success par highly focused hona chahiye aur project ki importance samajhni chahiye. Agar pehle project mein kuch dikhaya nahi to future initiatives khatre mein pad sakte hain.

Leader ko business ya operational background hona chahiye, saath mein kuch technical skills bhi. Woh business case pehchan sake aur vision ko IT department aur senior management ko communicate kar sake.

Technical logon mein PhD zaroori nahi hai. PhD log brilliant hote hain, lekin woh innovations par focus karte hain — models refine karna ya naye banana. Pilot ke liye yeh skills essential nahi hain.

Software engineering ya data science background wale log chahiye. Lekin unhe bhi AI ki training chahiye ho sakti hai — kuch mahine ML aur DL ke core principles seekhne mein, aur TensorFlow jaise platforms use karne mein.

Consultants ki madad bhi le sakte ho — AI opportunities pehchanne, data preparation aur models banane mein.

Team mein risk lene wale aur open-minded log hone chahiye — warna progress bahut mushkil hogi.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 8
← PreviousStep 1 — Problem pehchano (pehla AI project chunne ke 4 rules)Next →Step 3 — Tools aur platforms (Python aur Zen of Python)
8.7Chapter 8 — Implementation of AI

Step 3 — Tools aur platforms (Python aur Zen of Python)

AI models banane ke tools zyadatar open source hain. Pehle IT assessment karo — phir tools evaluate karo. Company mein pehle se hi multiple AI tools ho sakte hain — integration aur management ki problems hoti hain. Isi liye AI Tools stack ki strategy banao.

Python Language: ek researcher ne 1980s ke end mein Python banayi — naam British comedy series Monty Python se aaya. Python AI development ka standard ban gayi.

Simplicity ki wajah se — kuch lines mein sophisticated models ban jate hain (filter, map, reduce jaise functions). Lekin sophisticated coding bhi possible hai.

Zen of Python (philosophy):

  • Beautiful is better than ugly.
  • Explicit is better than implicit.
  • Simple is better than complex.
  • Complex is better than complicated.
  • Flat is better than nested.
  • Sparse is better than dense.

Python academic community mein grow hui — Internet se distribution tez hui, aur thousands of AI packages/libraries ka ecosystem ban gaya:

  • NumPy: scientific computing — high-performance arrays, high-end data processing ke liye critical.
  • Matplotlib: datasets plot karo; NumPy/Pandas ke saath use hoti hai. Pandas = "Python Data Analysis Library" — data structures banane mein aasan.
  • SimpleAI: ek mashhoor AI kitab (Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach) ke algorithms ka implementation.
  • PyBrain: modular ML library — neural networks aur reinforcement learning, kam coding mein.
  • Scikit-Learn (2007): regression, clustering aur classification.

Seekhne ke resources: YouTube par thousands of free courses. Doosri languages bhi hain — C++, C#, Java — zyada powerful lekin complex. Models banane ke liye full-fledged applications ki zaroorat nahi hoti. GPUs ke liye CUDA Python bhi hai.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 8
← PreviousStep 2 — Team banao (two-pizza rule)Next →AI Frameworks — TensorFlow, PyTorch, Keras, Jupyter
8.8Chapter 8 — Implementation of AI

AI Frameworks — TensorFlow, PyTorch, Keras, Jupyter

AI frameworks end-to-end systems hain — models banao, train karo, deploy karo. Sabse popular hai TensorFlow (Google backed).

Google ne 2011 mein Google Brain division se TensorFlow develop karna shuru kiya — neural networks tez banane ke liye. 2015 mein open source kar diya — taaki AI ki progress tez ho. Result: industry standard ban gaya. 41 million+ downloads, 1,800+ contributors. TensorFlow Lite (embedded systems ke liye) 2 billion+ mobile devices par chal raha hai.

Ecosystem: TensorFlow Federated (decentralized data), TensorFlow Privacy, TensorFlow Probability, TensorFlow Agents (reinforcement learning), Mesh TensorFlow (massive datasets).

Languages: Swift, JavaScript, R — lekin sabse common Python hai. Structure: input data multidimensional array hota hai — tensor. Commands C++ kernel se process hote hain — high performance ke liye.

TensorFlow se kya-kya bana:

  • Ek national lab ke researchers ne extreme weather predict karne ka DL system banaya — pehla model jisne exa (1 billion billion calculations) barrier toda. Gordon Bell Prize jeeta.
  • Airbnb ne millions of listing photos categorize kiye — guest experience aur conversions badhe.
  • Google ne NASA ke Kepler telescope ka data analyse kiya — neural network ne 2 exoplanets discover kiye. Code public kar diya.

Google TensorFlow 2.0 par kaam kar raha tha — API simpler banana, Datasets se data preparation streamline karna.

Doosre frameworks:

  • PyTorch (Facebook, 2016): runner-up. Intuitive interface, dynamic computation graphs — runtime mein models change kar sakte ho. Different back-end CPUs/GPUs support karta hai.
  • Keras: beginners ke liye. Thode se Python code mein neural networks. Docs mein likha hai: "Keras is an API designed for human beings, not machines. It puts user experience front and center." 30-second "Getting Started" guide! Lekin powerful bhi hai — TensorFlow ne Keras ko integrate kar liya. Pros bhi initial experimentation ke liye use karte hain.

Jupyter Notebook: platform nahi, web app hai — Python aur R mein code likho, visualizations banao, AI systems import karo. Kaam share karna aasan hai — GitHub jaisa.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 8
← PreviousStep 3 — Tools aur platforms (Python aur Zen of Python)Next →AutoML aur low-code — citizen data scientist
8.9Chapter 8 — Implementation of AI

AutoML aur low-code — citizen data scientist

Nayi category hai Automated Machine Learning (autoML) — data prep aur feature selection jaise processes handle karta hai. Goal: un organizations ki madad karna jinke paas experienced data scientists nahi hain. Is trend ko "citizen data scientist" kehte hain — bina strong technical background ke useful models banao.

Players: H2O.ai, DataRobot, SaaS. Drag-and-drop se models banao. Facebook aur Google ne apne teams ke liye autoML banaye — Facebook ka Asimo har mahine 300,000 models train aur test karta hai.

Lenovo Brazil ka case: supply chain predict karne ke ML models banane mein mushkil thi. 2 log har hafte 1,500 lines R code likhte the — kaafi nahi tha. Data scientists hire karna cost-effective nahi tha. DataRobot implement kiya — automation se zyada variables wale models bane, behtar results mile. Kuch mahino mein DataRobot users 2 se 10 ho gaye.

TasksBeforeAfter
Model creation4 weeks3 days
Production models2 days5 minutes
Accuracy of predictions<80%87.5%

Table 8-1: autoML implement karne ke results — Lenovo Brazil.

Caveats: Lenovo ke paas skilled data scientists the. Bina expertise ke autoML use karo to faulty assumptions/data wale models ban sakte hain — results AI na use karne se bhi bure ho sakte hain! Isi liye DataRobot pehle saal ke liye dedicated field engineer aur data scientist deta hai.

Low-code platforms: Appian leader hai — guarantee hai "Idea to app in eight weeks." Data structure clean setup karo, issues par alerts milte hain. Alag AI platforms (Google, Amazon, Microsoft) ko test karke best chuno. Modern interface ke saath Web ya mobile apps par deploy karo.

KPMG ka case: clients ko LIBOR se transition karwana tha. Apne AI platform Ignite se unstructured data ingest kiya, ML + NLP se contracts remediate kiye. Phir Appian se document sharing, customizable business rules aur real-time reporting. Manual process mein hazaron ghante aur 10–15% error rate — Ignite/Appian se accuracy 96% se zyada, aur documents seconds mein process hue.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 8
← PreviousAI Frameworks — TensorFlow, PyTorch, Keras, JupyterNext →Deploy aur monitor karo — change management
8.10Chapter 8 — Implementation of AI

Deploy aur monitor karo — change management

Model ban gaya — ab deploy aur monitor karna hai. Iske liye change management chahiye — hamesha complex aur difficult hota hai. AI typical IT implementation se alag hai — predictions aur insights se decisions lene hote hain. Logon ko technology se interact karne ka tareeka dobara sochna padta hai.

End-users aam taur par non-technical honge — employees ya consumers. Isi liye model ko aasan banana zaroori hai. Example: online marketing system mein options ko sirf 4–5 tak limit karo. Zyada options hon to users frustrate ho jate hain — "analysis paralysis" problem. Adoption kam ho jata hai.

Interactive visualizations use karo — variables adjust karke trends dekho, chart par click karke drill down karo.

Documentation banao — sirf likhit nahi, video tutorials bhi. Adoption badhane mein bahut madad milti hai.

Best practice: initial deployment limited rakho — chhote beta users group aur customer base ka chhota hissa. Warning do ki AI model early stages mein hai, bugs ho sakte hain. Yeh phase learning ka hai — kya kaam karta hai? Kya hatana hai? Kya sudharna hai? Iterative process hai — jaldi mat karo.

Full deployment ke waqt support aur project lead hona chahiye. Team ko recognition mile — ideally sabse upar ke levels se — taaki aur innovation encourage ho.

Workflow streamline karne ke platforms: Alteryx — vision hai data science aur analytics ko democratize karna, technical background ho ya na ho. Data discovery, data preparation, analytics aur deployment — sab code-free drag-and-drop se. Customers: Hyatt, Unilever, Kroger jaise non-technology operators.

AI development ek journey hai — strategy badalti rahegi. Ek data platform ke VP ne kaha: "What businesses sometimes fail to realize is that the path to AI is a long-term evolution of not only technology but in the way the company collaborates and works together. So, in addition to education, one of the key components to an AI strategy should be overall change management. It is important to create both short- and long-term roadmaps of what will be accomplished with first maybe predictive analytics, then perhaps machine learning, and ultimately — as a longer-term goal — AI, and how each roadmap impacts various pieces of the business as well as people who are a part of those business lines and their day-to-day work."

Chapter 8 ke Key Takeaways: Best companies ko bhi AI implement karne mein mushkil hoti hai — planning aur diligence chahiye, failure common hai. 2 tareeke: vendor software ya in-house model. Off-the-shelf apps mein bhi kaam hai — employees sahi data input karein to hi results sahi honge. Education critical hai — experienced engineers ke liye bhi. Bias, security aur privacy ke risks ko dhyaan mein rakho. Steps: problem pehchano, team banao, tools chuno, model banao, deploy aur monitor karo. Log aur technology ka "tango" samjho. Popular tools: TensorFlow, PyTorch, Python, Keras, Jupyter Notebook. AutoML beginners ki madad karta hai. Deployment sirf scaling nahi — easy to use bhi hona chahiye taaki adoption ho.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 8
← PreviousAutoML aur low-code — citizen data scientistNext →Bhavishya — ummeed ya darr?
9.1Chapter 9 — The Future of AI

Bhavishya — ummeed ya darr?

Late 2017 mein Web Summit conference mein ek legendary physicist ne AI ke future par apni rai di. Ek taraf ummeed thi — AI human intelligence se aage nikal sakti hai, horrible diseases cure ho sakti hain, climate change jaise environmental problems solve ho sakte hain.

Doosri taraf dark side bhi tha — unhone kaha ki AI "worst event in the history of our civilization" (hamari sabhyata ki sabse buri ghatna) bhi ho sakti hai. Problems: mass unemployment aur killer robots. Isi liye unhone AI ko control karne ka tareeka dhoondhne ki baat ki.

Yeh vichaar fringe (kinare wale) nahi hain — do mashhoor tech entrepreneurs ne bhi AI par gehri chinta jatai hai.

Doosri taraf optimists bhi hain — ek bade venture fund ($100 billion Vision fund) ke CEO ne CNBC interview mein kaha ki 30 saalon mein flying cars hongi, log zyada jeeyenge aur kai diseases cure ho jayengi. Unke fund ka main focus AI hai.

Kaun sahi hai — dystopian ya utopian? Ya beech mein kuch? Technology predict karna bahut mushkil hai, lagbhag impossible. Galat predictions ke examples:

  • Ek mashhoor inventor ne kaha tha AC (alternating current) fail ho jayega.
  • Ek mashhoor tech company ke co-founder ki kitab The Road Ahead (late 1995) mein Internet ka zikr hi nahi tha.
  • 2007 mein BlackBerry ke co-CEO ne kaha tha iPhone ko traction nahi milegi.
  • Blade Runner movie (1982, 2019 mein set) mein video phones wale phone booths aur insaan jaise androids ("replicants") predict kiye gaye the — dono galat nikle.

Ek cheez certain hai — aane wale saalon mein AI se bahut innovation aur change hoga. Industry mein huge investments ho rahe hain.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 9
← PreviousDeploy aur monitor karo — change managementNext →Autonomous Cars — Stanford Cart se Dickmanns tak
9.2Chapter 9 — The Future of AI

Autonomous Cars — Stanford Cart se Dickmanns tak

Autonomous cars AI ka sabse far-reaching area hai. Yeh naya nahi hai — science fiction mein decades se hai. Lekin real-life examples bhi purane hain:

Stanford Cart: early 1960s mein shuru hua — pehle moon missions ke liye remote-controlled vehicle banana tha. Phir focus badla — basic autonomous vehicle banaya, cameras aur AI se navigation karta tha. Era ke hisaab se standout achievement tha, lekin practical nahi tha — har move plan karne mein 10+ minutes lagte the!

Ek German aerospace engineer: mid-1980s mein Mercedes van ko autonomous vehicle mein badla. Cameras, sensors aur computers jode. Software mein creative tareeka — sirf important visual details par graphics processing focus ki, taaki power bache. System steering, gas pedal aur brakes control karta tha. 1994 mein Paris highway par test kiya — 600+ miles, 81 MPH tak speed. Lekin funding kheench li gayi — commercialization timely nahi dikh raha tha, aur AI winter aa raha tha.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 9
← PreviousBhavishya — ummeed ya darr?Next →DARPA Grand Challenge aur car ke components
9.3Chapter 9 — The Future of AI

DARPA Grand Challenge aur car ke components

Autonomous cars ka inflection point 2004 mein aaya. Catalyst tha Iraq War — American soldiers par horrible toll pad raha tha. DARPA ko laga autonomous vehicles solution ho sakte hain.

DARPA ne contest banaya — DARPA Grand Challenge (2004), $1 million grand prize. Mojave Desert mein 150-mile race — koi bhi car finish nahi kar payi!

Lekin isse innovation aur badhi. Agle saal 5 cars ne race finish ki. 2007 tak cars U-turns aur merging jaise actions karne lagi.

Is process se autonomous vehicles ke key components bane:

  • Sensors: radar aur ultrasonic systems — vehicles aur obstacles (jaise curbs) detect karte hain.
  • Video Cameras: road signs, traffic lights aur pedestrians detect karte hain.
  • Lidar (Light Detection and Ranging): aam taur par car ke upar hota hai — laser beams se surroundings measure karta hai. Data existing maps mein integrate hota hai.
  • Computer: steering, acceleration aur braking control karta hai. AI se seekhta hai, aur objects avoid karne, laws follow karne ke built-in rules bhi hote hain.
SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 9
← PreviousAutonomous Cars — Stanford Cart se Dickmanns takNext →Autonomy ke 5 levels — Level 0 se Level 5 tak
9.4Chapter 9 — The Future of AI

Autonomy ke 5 levels — Level 0 se Level 5 tak

"Autonomous" ka matlab kya hai — yeh confuse karta hai. Kya car poori tarah khud chalegi, ya human driver bhi hoga? Iske liye 5 levels hain:

LevelMatlab
Level 0Human saare systems control karta hai
Level 1Computer limited functions control karta hai — jaise cruise control ya braking — lekin ek waqt mein ek hi
Level 2Car 2 functions automate kar sakti hai
Level 3Car saare safety functions automate karti hai — lekin driver intervene kar sakta hai agar kuch galat ho
Level 4Car aam taur par khud chal sakti hai — lekin kuch cases mein human ki zaroorat padti hai
Level 5Holy Grail — car poori tarah autonomous hai

Auto industry sabse bade markets mein se ek hai. Transportation household expenditure mein doosre number par hai — housing ke baad, healthcare se double. Aur typical car sirf 5% waqt use hoti hai — baaki waqt parked rehti hai!

Allied Market Research ke hisaab se autonomous vehicle market 2026 tak $556.67 billion tak pahunchega — 39.47% CAGR.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 9
← PreviousDARPA Grand Challenge aur car ke componentsNext →Self-driving cars ki challenges — 71% log darte hain
9.5Chapter 9 — The Future of AI

Self-driving cars ki challenges — 71% log darte hain

Self-driving cars kab mainstream honge? Estimates alag-alag hain. Ek car-sharing company ke CEO ne kaha: "At best, we are still years away from a car that doesn't require a steering wheel. Cars will still need to be insured, repaired, and maintained, even if you came back from the future in a Delorean and brought the manual for how to make these cars fully autonomous. We make 100 million cars-per-year, of which 16 million-a-year are in the U.S. And, supposing you wanted the whole supply to have these artificial intelligence features, it would still take 20 years until we had more cars on the road including all the different levels of A.I. versus the number of cars that didn't have those technologies."

Driving complex hai — khaas taur par urban aur suburban areas mein. Traffic sign badal jaye ya manipulate ho jaye to kya hoga? Autonomous car ko dilemma face karna pade to — oncoming car se takraye ya curb par chadhe jahan pedestrians hon? Yeh bahut mushkil faisle hain.

Simple tasks bhi tough hain — ek self-driving company ke CEO ne bataya ki parking lots prime example hain: available spots dhoondhna, doosri cars aur pedestrians (jo unpredictable hote hain) se bachna, aur space mein ghusna.

Technology ke alawa doosri challenges:

  • Infrastructure: cities traditional cars ke liye bani hain. Autonomous vehicles mix karne par logistical issues honge. Car human drivers ke actions kaise anticipate karegi? Roads ke saath sensors lagane padenge, ya autonomous vehicles ke liye alag roads. Driver's ed bhi badalni hogi.
  • Regulation: sabse bada wild card — governments slow kaam karti hain, change se resistant hoti hain. US highly litigious country hai — yeh bhi development ko rok sakta hai.
  • Adoption: autonomous vehicles saste nahi honge — Lidar jaise systems costly hain. Public mein skepticism bhi hai — AAA survey ke hisaab se lagbhag 71% respondents autonomous vehicle mein ride karne se darte hain.

Isi liye shuru mein autonomous vehicles controlled situations mein honge — trucking, mining ya shuttles. Example: ek energy company Canada mein autonomous trucks se excavation karti hai.

Ride-sharing networks (Uber, Lyft) bhi starting point ho sakte hain — fairly structured aur public ko samajh mein aane wala.

Waymo (Google) Phoenix: self-driving taxi service test kar rahi hai. Company ke blog ke hisaab se: "We'll start by giving riders access to our app. They can use it to call our self-driving vehicles 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. They can ride across several cities in the Metro Phoenix area, including Chandler, Tempe, Mesa, and Gilbert. Whether it's for a fun night out or just to get a break from driving, our riders get the same clean vehicles every time and our Waymo driver with over 10 million miles of experience on public roads. Riders will see price estimates before they accept the trip based on factors like the time and distance to their destination."

Waymo ne paya ki education key hai — riders ke bahut sawaal hote hain. App mein chat system banaya support person se contact karne ke liye. Car ke dashboard par screen hai jo ride ki details deti hai. Blog ke hisaab se: "Feedback from riders will continue to be vital every step of the way."

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 9
← PreviousAutonomy ke 5 levels — Level 0 se Level 5 takNext →US vs China — $150 billion ki race
9.6Chapter 9 — The Future of AI

US vs China — $150 billion ki race

China ki tezi astonishing hai — kuch saalon mein economy US se badi ho sakti hai, aur is growth ka key part AI hoga. Chinese government ne 2030 tak AI par $150 billion kharch karne ka ambitious goal rakha hai. Baidu, Alibaba aur Tencent jaise companies bhi major investments kar rahi hain.

China ko aksar "copycat" kaha jata hai — Silicon Valley jitna creative nahi mana jata. Lekin yeh perception myth ho sakti hai. Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence ki study ke hisaab se China US ko AI ke sabse zyada cited technical papers mein outrank karne wala hai.

China ke fayde (ek AI expert aur venture capitalist ki kitab AI Superpowers ke hisaab se):

  • Enthusiasm: 1950s mein Russia ke Sputnik ne US mein engineers banne ki interest jagayi thi. China mein waisa hi hua — jab desh ke top Go player ek AI system (AlphaGo) se haare, to yeh wake-up call tha. Kai young log AI mein career banane lage.
  • Data: population 1.3 billion se zyada, 700 million+ Internet users. Authoritarian government ki wajah se privacy ko zyada importance nahi di jati — AI models banane mein zyada leeway hai. Example: Nature Medicine mein ek paper mein Chinese researchers ko 600,000 patients ka data mila healthcare study ke liye. AI model bachchon ki conditions (flu, meningitis) effectively diagnose kar paya.
  • Infrastructure: government next-generation cities bana rahi hai — autonomous cars aur AI systems ke liye. 5G networks ka aggressive rollout bhi ho raha hai.

US mein government AI par zyada tentative rahi hai. President ne "American AI Initiative" executive order sign kiya — lekin terms vague hain aur kitna paisa commit hoga, yeh clear nahi hai.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 9
← PreviousSelf-driving cars ki challenges — 71% log darte hainNext →Technological Unemployment — kya AI jobs kha jayegi?
9.7Chapter 9 — The Future of AI

Technological Unemployment — kya AI jobs kha jayegi?

Technological unemployment ka concept ek mashhoor economist ne Great Depression ke dauraan diya tha — innovations se long-term job loss ho sakta hai. Lekin evidence elusive raha hai — automation ne manufacturing ko bahut affect kiya, lekin workforce adapt kar leta hai.

Lekin AI revolution alag ho sakti hai. California ke Governor ko darr tha ki state mein trucking aur warehousing mein massive unemployment ho sakta hai — aur jald hi.

Harvest CROO Robotics: ek robot (Harv) strawberries aur plants ko bina bruise kiye pick kar sakta hai. Abhi experimental phase mein hai, lekin tezi se improve ho raha hai. Expectation hai ki ek robot 30 logon ka kaam karega. Na wages, na labor liability.

AI sirf low-skilled jobs nahi — white-collar professions bhi affect ho sakte hain. In jobs ko automate karne ka incentive zyada hai kyunki compensation zyada hai.

Legal field: kai startups (Lawgood, NexLP, RAVN ACE) legal research aur contract review automate kar rahe hain. Systems perfect nahi hain, lekin volume bahut zyada process kar sakte hain — aur use hote-hote smart hote jate hain.

Job market dynamic hai — naye careers bhi banenge. AI assistive bhi hogi — employees ka kaam aasan karegi. Example: ek software startup ne sophisticated algorithms se paper-based floorplans ko digitally interactive floorplans mein badla — projects start aur complete karna aasan ho gaya.

Phir bhi, AI ka broad impact hoga. Manufacturing mein 1960s–1990s ke job losses ko dekho — Pew Research Center ke hisaab se pichle 40 saalon mein real wage growth lagbhag zero rahi hai. US mein wealth gap badha hai — ek economist ke hisaab se 0.1% population ke paas lagbhag 20% wealth hai.

Kya kiya ja sakta hai:

  • Education aur transition assistance: governments skills ki ongoing renewal mein madad karein. Ek badi tech company ki CEO ne kaha ki AI 5–10 saalon mein saare jobs badal degi. Unki company mein automation se HR department mein headcount 30% kam hua.
  • Basic income: sabko minimum compensation mile. Inequality kam hogi, lekin drawbacks hain — logon ko careers se pride aur satisfaction milti hai. Job na mile to morale par profound impact ho sakta hai.
  • AI tax: AI se fayda uthane wali companies se gains wapas lena. Lekin unki power ko dekhte hue aisa legislation pass karna tough hoga.
SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 9
← PreviousUS vs China — $150 billion ki raceNext →AI ka hathiyarkaran — killer robots aur nuclear war?
9.8Chapter 9 — The Future of AI

AI ka hathiyarkaran — killer robots aur nuclear war?

Air Force Research Lab Skyborg naam ke prototypes par kaam kar raha hai — Star Wars jaisa. Skyborg ko R2-D2 samjho jo fighter jet ke liye AI wingman hai — targets aur threats identify karta hai. Pilot incapacitated ya distracted ho to AI control bhi le sakta hai. Air Force drones operate karne ke liye bhi is technology ko dekh raha hai.

Cool hai — lekin bada issue hai: kya AI se humans ko battlefield par life-and-death decisions se bahar kar diya jayega? Kya isse zyada bloodshed hoga? Machines galat faisle lein to aur problems hongi?

Kai AI researchers aur entrepreneurs concerned hain — 2,400+ ne statement sign kiya hai jo robot killers par ban ki maang karta hai.

United Nations bhi ban explore kar raha hai. Lekin US, Australia, Israel, UK aur Russia ne iska virodh kiya hai. Result: asli AI arms race ubhar sakti hai.

RAND Corporation ke paper ke hisaab se technology se 2040 tak nuclear war bhi ho sakta hai. Kaise? AI se submarines aur mobile missile systems ko target karna aasan ho jayega. Report ke hisaab se: "Nations may be tempted to pursue first-strike capabilities as a means of gaining bargaining leverage over their rivals even if they have no intention of carrying out an attack, researchers say. This undermines strategic stability because even if the state possessing these capabilities has no intention of using them, the adversary cannot be sure of that."

Near term mein AI ka sabse zyada impact information warfare par hoga — jo bahut destructive ho sakta hai. 2016 presidential election mein ek desh ki government ne interfere kiya — approach low-tech thi (social media troll farms se fake news), lekin consequences significant the.

AI powerful aur affordable hote hi aise campaigns supercharge ho jayenge — deepfake systems se life-like photos aur videos banakar messages jaldi failaye ja sakte hain.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 9
← PreviousTechnological Unemployment — kya AI jobs kha jayegi?Next →Drug Discovery — AI se nayi dawaaiyan
9.9Chapter 9 — The Future of AI

Drug Discovery — AI se nayi dawaaiyan

Drug discovery mein advances miraculous rahi hain — hepatitis C jaisi diseases ke cures mil gaye, cancers mein strides hui hain. Lekin bahut kaam baaki hai — drug companies ko treatments banane mein mushkil ho rahi hai.

Example: March 2019 mein ek biotech company ki Alzheimer's drug (Phase III trials) meaningful results nahi dikha payi. News par company ke shares 29% gir gaye — $18 billion market value wipe out ho gayi.

Traditional drug development mein bahut trial and error hota hai — time-consuming. Kya behtar tareeka hai? Researchers AI ki taraf dekh rahe hain — kai startups is opportunity par kaam kar rahe hain.

Insitro: 2019 mein shuru hui, Series A mein $100 million raise kiye — investors mein Alexandria Venture Investments, Bezos Expeditions, Mubadala, Two Sigma Ventures aur Verily. Team chhoti hai (lagbhag 30 employees) lekin brilliant researchers hain — data science, deep learning, software engineering, bioengineering aur chemistry. CEO ko advanced computer science aur health sciences dono ka rare blend hai — Google ki healthcare business Calico ko lead kiya tha.

Insitro ne mega drug operator Gilead ke saath partnership ki — $1 billion se zyada potential payments, NASH (serious liver disease) par research ke liye. Gilead ke paas bahut data hai models train karne ke liye — cells outside the body (in vitro system) se. Gilead ko alternative approaches ki urgency hai — uski ek NASH treatment (selonsertib) clinical trials mein fail hui thi.

AI ki promise: deep learning complex patterns identify karke drug discovery tez karegi. Personalized treatments bhi ban sakti hain — vyakti ki genetic make-up ke hisaab se — jo certain diseases cure karne ke liye critical ho sakti hai.

Lekin expectations temper karo:

  • Healthcare industry ko badalna hoga — AI ki education badhegi, waqt lagega, resistance hogi.
  • Deep learning aam taur par "black box" hai — algorithms kaise kaam karte hain, samajhna mushkil. FDA ko causal relationships chahiye — regulatory approval mushkil ho sakta hai.
  • Human body highly sophisticated hai — hum abhi bhi seekh rahe hain. Human Genome decode karne ke baad bhi naye approaches samajhne mein waqt laga.

Complexities ka sign: IBM ka Watson — sabse talented AI researchers aur billions kharch karne ke bawajood, company ne drug discovery ke liye Watson bechna band kar diya.

SourceApress — Artificial Intelligence Basics: A Non-Technical Introduction (2019), Chapter 9
← PreviousAI ka hathiyarkaran — killer robots aur nuclear war?Next →Government aur regulation — Alexa, Rekognition, COMPAS
9.10Chapter 9 — The Future of AI

Government aur regulation — Alexa, Rekognition, COMPAS

April 2019 mein ek article ne hulchul macha di — ismein bataya gaya tha ki Amazon apne Alexa speaker AI system ko kaise manage karta hai. Algorithms ke saath-saath hazaron log voice clips analyse karte hain taaki results behtar hon — khaas taur par slang aur regional dialects ke nuances handle karne ke liye, jo deep learning ke liye mushkil hain.

Logon ne poocha: kya mera smart speaker sach mein sun raha hai? Kya meri conversations private hain?

Amazon ne kaha ki uske strict rules hain. Lekin article ke hisaab se AI reviewers ko kabhi-kabhi aise clips sunne ko milte the jinmein potentially criminal activity hoti thi, jaise sexual assault — lekin Amazon ki policy thi interfere na karna.

AI pervasive hote hi aisi kahaniyan aur aayengi — aur clear-cut answers nahi honge. Kuch log AI products khareedna band kar denge — lekin yeh chhota group hoga. Facebook ke privacy issues ke bawajood user growth mein kami nahi aayi.
